title: New Hancock Whitney logo and brand debut today
summary: Hancock Whitney, a leading financial institution in the United States, unveiled its new brand and logo on May 1, 2018, marking a significant milestone in its 100-year history. The bank, which merged Hancock Bank and Whitney Bank in 2011, officially changed its name to Hancock Whitney Bank on May 25, 2018. The new brand reflects the shared history of both institutions, emphasizing their commitment to clients, communities, and financial stability. The logo, which features a stylized 'HW' representing the bank's five core values, symbolizes the enduring relationship between the two banks. The brand update includes new signage at headquarters, regional offices, and over 260 ATMs, with additional changes to online and mobile banking, debit and credit cards, and checks within the next 60 days. The tagline 'Your Dream. Our Mission' underscores the bank's dedication to helping clients achieve their financial goals. Hancock Whitney, part of Hancock Holding Company, operates in multiple states and has been recognized as one of America's most financially sound banks for over a century.

title: Deere (DE) earnings Q1 2020
summary: Deere (DE) reported an unexpected increase in first-quarter profit for Q1 2020, with net income of $517 million, or $1.63 per share, compared to $498 million, or $1.54 per share, in the same period last year. This surpassed the average analyst estimate of $1.26 per share. The company retained its full-year earnings forecast of $2.7 billion to $3.1 billion for 2020. The rise in profits was attributed to stabilization in the U.S. farm sector, which offset weak demand for construction machines. Deere's shares rose 9% to $180.75 in premarket trade. The company's earnings were previously impacted by the U.S.-China trade war, but hopes for a trade deal with China have boosted expectations for recovery in farm machinery demand. CEO John May noted that farmer confidence has improved due to trade tensions easing and higher agricultural exports. Improved pricing power, lower production costs, and reduced warranty expenses contributed to higher operating profits in the farm and turf business, which accounts for nearly 60% of Deere's revenue.

summary: On April 12, 2021, Gregory F. Covino resigned as Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer of Novavax, Inc. (the “Company”) effective April 12, 2021. Mr. Covino will remain an executive advisor to the Company under a new employment arrangement. In connection with Mr. Covino’s resignation, the Company appointed John J. Trizzino, Executive Vice President, Chief Commercial Officer, and Chief Business Officer of the Company, to serve as interim Chief Financial Officer. Mr. Covino’s employment as an executive advisor of the Company will be on an at-will basis pursuant to an employment agreement, pursuant to which Mr. Covino is entitled to an annual base salary of $262,500.

title: Ford is basically giving up on US car business; GM isn't far behind
summary: Ford and General Motors are shifting their focus away from traditional passenger cars toward trucks, SUVs, and crossovers. Ford plans to reduce its North American passenger car lineup to just two models: the iconic Mustang and the Focus Active. GM is also moving in the same direction, with its CFO, Chuck Stevens, acknowledging the challenging environment for passenger cars. Despite this shift, sedans will still form a significant portion of U.S. vehicle sales for the foreseeable future. Crossover sales have been a key driver for GM's earnings, and the company is investing in new truck models to support its margins. Both companies are adapting to changing consumer preferences, with a clear emphasis on SUVs and crossovers. Ford is shifting its focus away from traditional sedans and toward SUVs, crossovers, and trucks, as the U.S. market increasingly favors these vehicle types. According to LMC Automotive, by 2025, 27% of U.S. vehicle sales will be cars, while 84% of GM's U.S. sales will be SUVs, crossovers, and trucks, and Ford will be at 90%. Chrysler is expected to reach 97%. This trend reflects a broader shift in the U.S. automotive industry, where American automakers are prioritizing SUVs and trucks over traditional sedans. Ford is doubling down on "authentic off-roaders," including the Raptor and the upcoming Bronco, while GM and Chrysler are also entering this segment. Ford's strategy involves creating new products that fill "white spaces" in the market, combining elements of cars and SUVs to differentiate its offerings. Analysts suggest that Ford's decision to pivot away from traditional sedans is a difficult but necessary move to remain competitive in a changing market.

summary: Nicholas Financial, Inc. (NASDAQ: NICK) reported its financial results for the three months ended December 31, 2016. Diluted earnings per share decreased by 40% to $0.21, compared to $0.35 for the same period in 2015. Net earnings were $1.6 million for the quarter ended December 31, 2016, down from $2.7 million in the same period of 2015. Revenue declined 3% to $22.0 million for the quarter ended December 31, 2016, compared to $22.8 million in the prior-year period. The results reflect the company's performance in its financial services operations during the quarter. The report was filed with the SEC on February 2, 2017, and includes a press release dated the same date. The company's management, including Ralph T. Finkenbrink and Katie L. MacGillivary, signed the report as required under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

title: Norwest Equity Partners Sells Stanton Carpet Corporation to Quad-C Management
summary: Norwest Equity Partners sold Stanton Carpet Corporation to Quad-C Management on November 21, 2016. Financial terms were not disclosed. Stanton Carpet Corporation is a leading value-added distributor of premium soft flooring products. The Stanton family of brands are available through approximately 4,000 retail partners nationwide, including independent retail floor showrooms, trade showrooms, and home furnishing retailers. Stanton currently employs more than 100 people. NEP worked closely with the Stanton management team over the last four years to achieve robust growth and position the Company for future success. Key growth initiatives were strategically focused on the continued build out of award winning products and brands, including the recent acquisition of Crescent Carpet, the expansion of the Company's sales force, international supply partners, and showroom and retail partners. Stanton recently completed the construction of a new distribution facility in Calhoun, Georgia to support current and future growth.

title: Testimony by Vice Chair for Supervision Quarles on supervision and regulation - Federal Reserve Board
summary: On May 19, 2021, Federal Reserve Vice Chair Quarles testified about the U.S. banking sector's recovery post-COVID-19. The banking system, strengthened by over 10 years of reforms, absorbed unprecedented shocks while supporting public aid and borrowers. The recovery was aided by coordinated efforts from Congress and the Federal Reserve. Post-2008 reforms ensured a different outcome compared to the 2008 crisis. The Federal Reserve Board emphasized that the banking system is more liquid and better capitalized than a year ago, with over $100 billion in additional loan loss reserves. The system is well-positioned to weather future shocks. While a strong recovery is underway, it is not yet complete. Policymakers aim to support the financial system and economy through the transition back to normal operations. The Fed has aligned emergency actions with other relief efforts, maintained or extended some measures to preserve household assistance and promote credit access, and begun transitioning back to normal supervisory activities. These steps are part of a responsible transition out of the emergency posture.

events.quote: The economy is beginning a strong recovery, which owes much to an extraordinary, coordinated, and sustained campaign of support, by both Congress and the Federal Reserve
banking organizations have remained an important source of strength in this recovery

events.key_values: over $100 billion in additional loan loss reserves
events.quote: banking system is actually more liquid and better capitalized than it was a year ago, with over $100 billion in additional loan loss reserves
The COVID event was a unique shock, but it was also the first real-world test of the regulatory and supervisory regime established after the 2008 financial crisis.
The stress-testing program not only prepared banks for a period of prolonged hardship; it also clarified their health and resilience as the COVID event progressed.
We can have particular confidence in the framework when it is supplemented and informed by a real-time stress testing regime.
Continued use of LIBOR in new contracts after 2021 would create safety and soundness risks

summary: NOVAVAX INC and Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd., a company incorporated under the laws of India, entered into a Second Amended and Restated Joint Venture Agreement for CPL Biologicals Private Limited. CPLB concurrently entered into Second Amended and Restated Product License Agreements with both the Company and Cadila as parts of the Amended Joint Venture Agreement. The Agreements permit CPLB to develop and commercialize certain Cadila biological products and to develop certain products using Novavax’ nanoparticle vaccine production, antigen specific seed development, protein expression, and cloning system technology. NOVAVAX INC and CPLB have clarified their rights of first negotiation regarding products developed or commercialized using each other's technology. The agreements also outline the initial development of four vaccine candidate seeds by NOVAVAX on behalf of CPLB. Ownership rights and percentages remain unchanged. The agreements are referenced in the Company’s 10-Q filing for the quarter ending September 30, 2018.

events.quote: The Agreements also clarify the Company’s rights of first negotiation with respect to any products CPLB develops and/or commercializes using the Company’s technology
The Agreements provide for the initial development by the Company on behalf of CPLB of four vaccine candidate seeds to be mutually determined

summary: On March 10, 2015, Optical Cable Corporation issued a press release announcing its first quarter of fiscal year 2015 financial results. The financial results and earnings call provide insights into the company's operational performance and financial condition during the first quarter of fiscal year 2015, which may influence market perceptions and future investment decisions related to Optical Cable Corporation.

title: US Bank Industry Earnings Highest Since 2006: FDIC
summary: The U.S. banking industry recorded its highest earnings since before the 2007-2009 financial crisis in 2012, according to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. Full-year earnings reached $141.3 billion, a 19.3 percent increase from 2011. The FDIC attributed much of the growth to reduced loan loss provisions and gains from loan sales and higher servicing income. In the fourth quarter of 2012, earnings totaled $34.7 billion, up 36.9 percent from the same period in 2011. Net operating revenue rose 4.5 percent to $169 billion. While the report signals recovery from the financial crisis, some larger banks cut jobs to address persistent challenges like declining trading volumes.

summary: Frost & Sullivan highlights the growing influence of women in the automotive industry, noting that female driving license holders in the U.S. now outnumber men at 51 percent, a trend expected to spread to Canada and the U.K. by 2016. Women are increasingly shaping car purchasing decisions, with 80 percent of buying decisions influenced by them. They prioritize practicality, freedom, and design, favoring smaller, maneuverable vehicles with advanced features like park assist and digital assistants. Women also show a preference for luxury brands and are more influenced by celebrity endorsements. Frost & Sullivan predicts that future cars will be more personalized, with a focus on safety, sustainability, and technology. The analysis underscores broader societal shifts, including increased female education, narrowing pay gaps, and rising female wealth, which are accelerating this trend in the automotive sector.

summary: BLONDER TONGUE LABORATORIES INC held its 2021 Annual Meeting of Stockholders on May 26, 2021, with a record date of April 15, 2021, and 11,960,505 shares of common stock outstanding. Shareholders voted on the election of directors and the ratification of the independent registered public accounting firm. Three nominees were elected as Class II directors, each serving a three-year term expiring at the 2024 annual meeting. Stockholders approved a proposal to ratify the appointment of Marcum LLP, certified public accountants, as the Company’s independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2021.

title: How GE Went From American Icon to Astonishing Mess - Bloomberg
summary: General Electric Co. (GE) has been a symbol of American innovation and corporate success for over a century. From the invention of the lightbulb to the development of jet engines and industrial plastics, GE has played a pivotal role in shaping modern technology and daily life. Throughout its 126-year history, the company has exemplified the power of corporate capitalism, manufacturing consumer products, industrial machinery, and even producing romantic comedies. GE has also contributed to significant historical events, including world wars, and has consistently rewarded investors despite economic downturns and technological disruptions. However, the article highlights a shift from this legacy of success to a more complex and challenging situation, setting the stage for a deeper exploration of GE's transformation.

summary: SanDisk Corporation released its Q4'13 and FY13 earnings report on January 22, 2014. The report includes both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures. The non-GAAP results exclude certain expenses, gains, and losses, such as share-based compensation and amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets. These non-GAAP measures are intended to provide a clearer view of the company's core operating performance and are consistent with financial models used by analysts. The report is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and is incorporated by reference. SanDisk Corporation released its Q4'13 earnings on January 22, 2014. The report highlights the use of non-GAAP financial measures, which the company believes provide consistency in financial reporting. These measures include the impact of the company's call option, which offsets the issuance of dilutive shares from its 1.5% Sr. Convertible Notes due 2017. The company also mentions the exclusion of non-cash charges such as amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, impairment of acquisition-related intangible assets, share-based compensation, and non-cash economic interest expense associated with convertible debt. These non-GAAP measures are used by management for assessing performance, allocating resources, and planning future periods. The report also notes that these measures should not be considered a substitute for GAAP results. The press release is included as an exhibit and is deemed to be 'furnished' rather than 'filed' for regulatory purposes.

summary: On April 24, 2012, OYO Geospace Corporation entered into a Second Amendment to Loan Agreement, effective as of March 31, 2012. The amendment, attached as Exhibit 10.1, modified the Loan Agreement with The Frost National Bank to exclude rental equipment investments from capital expenditure calculations for cash flow coverage ratio compliance. This change affects the company's financial covenant compliance under the loan agreement.

summary: This report is a Form 6-K filing by Royal Bank of Canada, a Canadian financial institution, detailing the issuance of various senior global medium-term notes. The filing includes information about the reverse convertible notes linked to Cliffs Natural Resources Inc. and direct investment notes linked to the EquityCompass Equity Risk Management Strategy. The notes were priced on March 5, 2012, and settled on March 8, 2012, with principal amounts of $500,000 and $4,500,000 respectively. The report also includes legal opinions from Norton Rose Canada LLP and Morrison & Foerster LLP regarding the validity of the notes under Canadian and New York law. The filing is part of the Bank’s shelf registration statement on Form F-3 (File No. 333-171806).

title: Sony profits rise 346% thanks to strong performance from PlayStation
summary: Sony reported a significant rise in profits, with a 346.4% increase in operating profit for its fiscal second quarter, driven by strong performance from the PlayStation gaming business and semiconductor division. The company's sales reached 2.06 trillion Japanese yen, surpassing expectations, and operating profit hit 204 billion yen, up from 135.6 billion yen. Sony also raised its dividend to 12.50 Japanese yen. The PlayStation division saw a 35.4% year-on-year rise in operating revenue, with a 188.3% increase in operating income. Major game titles like "FIFA 18" and "Unchartered: The Lost Legacy" contributed to this growth. Sony's semiconductor business also improved, with a profit of 49.4 billion yen, up from a 4.2 billion yen loss in the same period the previous year. The company's shares rose 2.7% following the results, and the stock has gained around 35% year-to-date. Sony reported a significant increase in profits, rising by 346%, largely due to the strong performance of its PlayStation division. The company has been focusing on innovation in areas such as virtual reality (VR) and artificial intelligence (AI). Sony CEO Kazuo Hirai emphasized the importance of innovation, stating that the company is committed to creating both traditional and new, sometimes wacky, products that excite consumers. This strategic focus on innovation and technology has contributed to Sony's recent financial success.

summary: Tucson Electric Power Company proposed an Environmental Compliance Adjustor (ECA) mechanism to recover environmental compliance costs, capped at 0.25% of total retail revenue requirement. The Energy Efficiency Resource Plan (EERP) allows TEP to invest in approved energy efficiency programs, with costs recoverable through existing demand-side management surcharge if targets are met. TEP entered into a 2013 Settlement Agreement with Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) and others regarding its rate case. The agreement requires ACC approval for new rates, with residential bills increasing by less than $3.00/month. Key terms include a non-fuel retail base rate increase of ~$76 million, OCRB of $1.5 billion, FVRB of $2.3 billion, weighted average cost of capital of 7.26%, return on equity of 10.0%, and a Lost Fixed Cost Recovery mechanism (LFCR) to recover non-fuel costs from lost kWh sales due to energy efficiency compliance. The agreement includes modifications to TEP’s Purchased Power and Fuel Adjustment clause (PPFAC).

title: Financing, Recognitions, and Announcements by Life Insurance Companies - Research Report on MetLife, Prudential, Lincoln National, Genworth, and Torchmark
summary: The report highlights key developments by major life insurance companies in the U.S. on December 2, 2013. MetLife, Inc. (MET) saw its stock decline by 0.25% on November 27, 2013, with a 0.47% drop over three trading days, compared to the Dow Jones Industrial Average's 0.20% rise. Prudential Financial, Inc. (PRU) announced a $324 million financing deal with Q-Park, securing 13 parking facilities in the Netherlands. The loan has a five-year term, predominantly fixed rate, and marks Prudential's second mortgage loan in continental Europe since 2012. Lincoln National Corp. (LNC) saw its stock rise 1.18% on November 27, 2013, with a 2.10% increase over three trading days, outperforming the S&P 500's 0.14% rise. Genworth Financial Inc. (GNW) recognized its CEO, Thomas J. McInerney, as part of Fortune's "Top 50 Business People," noting his 124% profit increase for the first nine months of 2013. Torchmark Corp. (TMK) was also mentioned but no specific details were provided.

title: The Fed - Supervisory Letter SR 16-17 on Supervisory Expectations for Risk Management of Reserve-Based Energy Lending Risk -- December 1, 2016
summary: The Federal Reserve issued Supervisory Letter SR 16-17 on December 1, 2016, outlining supervisory expectations for risk management in reserve-based energy lending. This guidance applies to state member banks, U.S. branches of foreign banking organizations, and depository institution holding companies involved in energy lending. The letter aims to enhance existing energy lending guidance and update financial institutions on key risks and risk management factors for reserve-based lending activities. Reserve-based lending involves financing secured by oil and gas reserves, with loan amounts determined by the borrower's proved reserves, adjusted for risk factors. The guidance emphasizes the need for robust risk management programs, including timely market condition analysis to support credit risk management and underwriting practices. Prolonged declines in crude oil prices can significantly impact reserve collateral values and cash flows, affecting the repayment ability of borrowers. Financial institutions are advised to monitor market factors such as oil and gas commodity prices, global supply and demand imbalances, and other relevant indicators to better manage and control their reserve-based lending portfolios. The letter also highlights the need for robust risk management programs, including concentration limits, market condition analysis, and integration into capital planning practices. Institutions should regularly review their policies and maintain capital levels commensurate with their reserve-based lending exposure. The letter emphasizes the need for institutions to separately manage troubled reserve-based loans where borrowers cannot generate sufficient cash flow from oil and/or gas production to repay the loan. These loans, sometimes called 'stretched' reserve-based loans, reflect borrowers with credit or liquidity weaknesses. Institutions should understand the fundamental causes of these weaknesses and may still work with troubled borrowers to service existing loans. The credit administration process should monitor exposure to the borrower, adjust credit facility ratings, and assess whether advancing additional funds is appropriate. Additional funds should aim to improve the borrower's financial condition. Risk management expectations vary based on the institution's specific risk characteristics, complexity, and size. Higher expectations are placed on institutions with significant reserve-based lending exposures in concentrated geographic locations and market segments. Institutions should also assess the impact of their reserve-based lending activities on their overall financial condition, including capital, allowance for loan and lease losses, and liquidity.

title: sgmo-20210122
summary: Sangamo Therapeutics, Inc. announced that Sung Lee, Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer, and Principal Financial Officer, notified the company of his resignation from these positions and employment, effective February 1, 2021. On January 22, 2021, the company and Mr. Lee entered into a letter agreement, under which Mr. Lee will serve as an independent contractor from February 2 to February 26, 2021. During this period, he will no longer serve as Chief Financial Officer but will continue as Principal Financial Officer in a consulting role, assisting with financial transition activities, including the filing of the 2020 Annual Report on Form 10-K. His compensation for this role will be a lump sum payment of $215,000 on February 26, 2021, which will be considered an annual cash bonus under the Amended and Restated Incentive Compensation Plan, subject to legal conditions.

title: Juul e-cigarettes' popularity among teens concerns schools, FDA
summary: Juul, a leading e-cigarette company, has become a major concern for schools and the FDA due to its popularity among teenagers. Despite Juul's claim that its products are intended for adult smokers, the brand has gained significant traction among high school and middle school students. The rise in Juul use has led to increased scrutiny from regulators, parents, and educators. Schools are implementing measures such as air detectors to monitor vaping activity, as seen in Plainedge High School in New York. Juul's market share has surged to 71% according to Nielsen, with sales increasing nearly 800% over the past year. The company has a valuation of $15 billion, but its popularity among teens has sparked debates about its impact on youth nicotine addiction. Critics argue that Juul's product design and flavors, such as creme brulee and mango, make it appealing to younger users. The CDC reports that the rate of high school cigarette smoking has dropped to 8.8%, but e-cigarettes have become the most popular tobacco product among teens. Teachers and administrators are struggling to address the widespread use of Juul, as it has become a common trend across various social groups. Schools are taking proactive measures by educating students, parents, and teachers about the risks of e-cigarette use. Some schools, like Plainedge High School, have installed vaping detectors, with Soter Technologies reporting over 1,000 contract proposals for the $995 device. While these measures aim to deter youth use, the issue has overshadowed stories of adults using Juul as a smoking alternative. Travis Barker, a digital sculptor, transitioned from traditional cigarettes to Juul after struggling with health issues from smoking. Juul markets its products to adult smokers, and the FDA is considering reducing nicotine levels in conventional cigarettes while providing alternatives like e-cigarettes. However, the agency faces pressure to regulate youth access to Juul and other e-cigarettes, with Massachusetts investigating the company for failing to prevent minors from purchasing its products. The FDA is also launching campaigns to address youth vaping and may require Juul's approval for its products to remain on the market. The FDA has extended the deadline for Juul and other e-cigarette manufacturers to submit their products for review until 2022. During this evaluation, the agency will assess the overall public health benefits of these products, with a significant focus on underage use. FDA Chief Scott Gottlieb emphasized that manufacturers must take more steps to address youth use to remain on the market. Juul, which has been in the U.S. market for three years, saw its retail sales reach $1.11 billion in 2018, with a market share of 71% as of that year. The company plans to expand overseas, having already launched in Israel, England, and Scotland, with Asia next on the agenda. Despite efforts to prevent underage use, including a $30 million investment in education and research, Juul continues to face criticism and legal challenges. At least three lawsuits have been filed against the company, alleging it marketed its products to young people and addicted them to nicotine. Juul denies the allegations and plans to defend the cases vigorously.

summary: The Walt Disney Company approved amendments to its Restated Certificate of Incorporation at its annual meeting on March 3, 2016. The amendments became effective after being filed with the Delaware Secretary of State. The amendments are detailed in the proxy statement dated January 15, 2016, and are incorporated by reference. The final voting results showed that the election of directors and the ratification of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP received more votes 'for' than 'against.' The advisory vote on executive compensation and the amendments to the Restated Certificate of Incorporation were approved by more than a majority and more than two-thirds of shares, respectively. Two shareholder proposals, a simple majority vote and lobbying disclosure, failed due to lack of majority support. The report was signed by Roger J. Patterson on March 4, 2016.

summary: The Subaru PUMA RallyCross Team confirmed they will compete in the remaining two Global RallyCross rounds with two of three team cars, using drivers Sverre Isachsen and Bucky Lasek. The decision to reduce the number of cars from three to two after Round 7 in Atlanta was made early in the season due to the GRC expanding its calendar to nine rounds from six. The team will release driver Dave Mirra from his contractual obligations if he seeks other opportunities. The team carries strong momentum after back-to-back podiums at X Games and Atlanta with driver Sverre Isachsen. The team races the 2013 Subaru WRX STI featuring Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive and a turbocharged boxer engine. The team has announced a two-car lineup to conclude the 2013 Global RallyCross season, marking the end of their participation in the rallycross series for the year. The details of the lineup and specific cars involved were not disclosed in the announcement. The team's participation reflects their commitment to high-performance racing and brand presence in motorsport events. The conclusion of the 2013 season sets the stage for future competitions and potential changes in the team's strategy for the upcoming season.

title: SEC.gov | SEC Adopts Rules to Implement FAST Act Mandate to Modernize and Simplify Disclosure
summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has adopted rules to modernize and simplify disclosure requirements for public companies, investment advisers, and investment companies, as mandated by the Fixing America’s Surface Transportation (FAST) Act. These amendments aim to eliminate outdated and unnecessary disclosures, improve readability and navigability of company disclosures, and reduce the burden on registrants. Key changes include increased flexibility in discussing historical periods in Management’s Discussion and Analysis, the ability to redact confidential information from most exhibits without a confidential treatment request, and the incorporation of technology to enhance access to information on the cover page of filings. The amendments will take effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register, with some provisions, such as data tagging and HTML formatting, having specific effective dates. The SEC emphasized that these changes will benefit investors by improving transparency and reducing costs. The SEC has adopted rules to implement the FAST Act mandate, aiming to modernize and simplify disclosure processes. The requirements for tagging data on the cover pages of certain filings are subject to a three-year phase-in period, depending on the nature of the filer. All investment company registration statements and Form N-CSR filings made on or after April 1, 2020, must be submitted in HTML format and comply with the rule and form amendments related to the use of hyperlinks. This update is part of the SEC's ongoing efforts to enhance transparency and efficiency in financial disclosures. The final rule was published in the Federal Register on March 20, 2019.

title: Bristol-Myers Squibb shares fall on $74 billion Celgene acquisition
summary: Bristol-Myers Squibb shares fell on the announcement of its $74 billion acquisition of Celgene, a move that has raised concerns among investors. The deal, valued at $74 billion and including $50 in cash and one share of Bristol-Myers Squibb per Celgene share, represents a significant financial commitment. The acquisition is expected to add $32 billion in fresh debt to Bristol-Myers Squibb's balance sheet, increasing its long-term obligations from $7.3 billion to over $52 billion. The deal also raises the cost to insure Bristol-Myers Squibb's bonds to their highest point since May 2010. While the acquisition may help Bristol-Myers Squibb strengthen its position in the cancer drug market, some investors remain skeptical about the price tag and the risks involved. Bristol-Myers Squibb shares fell following the announcement of its $74 billion acquisition of Celgene. The deal comes amid competition with Merck's Keytruda, which has outperformed Bristol's Opdivo in clinical trials for advanced lung cancer. Celgene's Revlimid, its top-selling drug, is expected to lose patent protection by 2022, raising concerns about future revenue. Analysts noted the overlap between the two companies and questioned whether the acquisition would solve long-term challenges for Bristol. Celgene has faced challenges with its recent acquisitions, including safety concerns with Ozanimod and doubts about the profitability of Juno Therapeutics' therapies. The combined company is expected to have nine products with over $1 billion in annual sales, with potential growth in oncology, immunology, and cardiovascular disease. The deal, which was finalized in 2019, marked a significant move in the pharmaceutical industry. Analysts noted that while there was initial disappointment from both companies, the long-term benefits of the merger were expected to outweigh the short-term challenges. The acquisition aimed to strengthen Bristol-Myers Squibb's position in the biopharmaceutical sector by combining Celgene's innovative drug development capabilities with the company's existing portfolio. The deal was seen as a bold strategic move, reflecting the competitive nature of the pharmaceutical market. The merger also raised questions about integration challenges and regulatory hurdles, which could impact the company's performance in the coming years.

summary: On November 17, 2014, Actavis plc ("Actavis") and Allergan, Inc. ("Allergan") issued a joint press release announcing the execution of an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "Merger Agreement") by and among Actavis, Allergan, and Avocado Acquisition Inc., a Delaware corporation and an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Actavis. The Merger Agreement is a significant development in the pharmaceutical industry, as it outlines the terms of a potential merger between two major players in the sector. The merger is expected to create a combined entity with a broader range of products and a stronger market position. The definitive joint proxy statement/prospectus will be delivered to shareholders of Actavis and Allergan, providing detailed information about the merger and its implications. Investors and security holders are urged to read the definitive joint proxy statement/prospectus and other documents that will be filed with the SEC. This Form 8-K filing from November 17, 2014, outlines the disclosure of information related to the merger between Actavis and Allergan. The document highlights that investors and security holders can access free copies of the registration statement and the definitive joint proxy statement/prospectus through the SEC's website. Actavis and Allergan have also provided access to their respective websites and investor relations departments for copies of the documents filed with the SEC. The filing notes that participants in the merger solicitation, including Actavis, Allergan, their directors, and certain executive officers, may be considered participants in the solicitation of proxies. The document also includes a cautionary statement regarding forward-looking statements, which are used to describe estimated or anticipated future results, including synergies, and reflect the company's current perspective as of the date of the communication.

summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. announced a reset dividend rate on its Series 38 and Series 25 Preference Shares. The filing indicates that the company is a foreign private issuer and that it files annual reports under Form 40-F. The dividend adjustment is a corporate action affecting the company's equity structure and shareholder returns. The change does not provide specific details on the new dividend rate or the rationale behind the adjustment. The filing does not mention any market impact or broader industry implications, focusing solely on the company's internal financial decisions.

title: Tula sees record sales in April even as coronavirus ravages retail
summary: Tula, a New York-based skincare company, reported record sales in April 2020, despite the challenges posed by the coronavirus pandemic. The company saw a 400% increase in sales compared to the previous year, marking its best April in six years. This growth was attributed to the rising demand for clean beauty products, which are free of toxic chemicals and undesirable ingredients like sulfates and parabens. Tula's CEO, Savannah Sachs, noted that consumers are increasingly investing in health and wellness while staying at home. The company's success is also linked to its direct-to-consumer (DTC) model and its focus on health-centered ingredients such as superfoods and probiotics. According to NPD, the natural beauty segment, including skincare, saw an 11% increase in sales, while prestige beauty sales dropped 14% in 2020. This trend highlights the growing importance of clean beauty in the market. Tula, a clean beauty brand, reported record sales in April despite the challenges posed by the coronavirus pandemic. The company's success is attributed to its strong social media presence and influencer partnerships. While Tula's sales grew significantly, it faced supply chain disruptions due to strict social distancing measures and reduced employee capacity in U.S. warehouses, leading to longer order processing times. The company's CEO, Sachs, emphasized the importance of transparent communication with customers during these disruptions. Tula also lost some exposure through its wholesale partnerships with retailers like Ulta and Nordstrom, which temporarily shut their doors. However, its strong ties to the influencer community helped it recover lost ground. Influencers with follower counts ranging from 2,000 to over 100,000 helped drive traffic and raise brand awareness. According to a 2019 survey by Euromonitor, 80% of respondents believe health-inspired beauty trends will influence sales in the next five years, highlighting the growing importance of clean beauty in the market.

title: For Biotech Takeovers, Timing Is Key
summary: Biotech and small drug companies are rarely acquired immediately before or after a drug approval or during the initial phase of a new drug launch. Vivus, which is awaiting FDA approval for its weight-loss drug Qnexa, may be in secret negotiations with a Big Pharma suitor. However, such a deal would be unusual. More likely, Vivus will launch the drug independently, and if sales boom, a suitor may come calling. Similar patterns are seen in past acquisitions, where biotech firms are typically acquired during mid- to late-stage clinical trials or after drug approval. Examples include Roche buying Inhibitex and Gilead Sciences acquiring Pharmasset. Other notable deals include Johnson & Johnson buying Cougar Biotech and Amgen acquiring Micromet. Companies like Eli Lilly and Takeda Pharmaceutical acquired firms after their drugs had years of sales. Forest Laboratories bought Clinical Data weeks after its antidepressant Viibryd received FDA approval. Amylin Pharmaceuticals, which recently launched Bydureon, also reportedly spurned a takeout offer from Bristol-Myers Squibb. These examples suggest that drug companies are often acquired after commercial launch, not during early stages of product development.

summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. announced on August 30, 2019, that it requested the delisting of all Class A Limited Voting Shares from Euronext Amsterdam due to low trading volume, costs, and administrative requirements. The company confirmed its shares will remain listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and Toronto Stock Exchange. Approval was received for the delisting, effective September 30, 2019, with the last trading date set for September 27, 2019. Shareholders holding Brookfield Euronext Shares can sell their shares on the NYSE and/or TSX. Shareholders may request additional information from their custodian and financial intermediary. Securities explicitly mentioned in the source include Brookfield Asset Management Inc. (BAM).

events.quote: Brookfield shares will remain listed on the New York Stock Exchange (“NYSE”) and Toronto Stock Exchange (“TSX”)
The Brookfield shares are expected to be delisted from Euronext Amsterdam, effective Monday September 30, 2019
The last trading date will be Friday September 27, 2019

summary: On July 24, 2019, Geospace Technologies Corporation issued a press release announcing its third quarter 2019 results and conference call schedule. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. Geospace Technologies (NASDAQ: GEOS) announced it will release third quarter fiscal year 2019 financial results on August 8, 2019, after the market closes. The company has scheduled a conference call for August 9, 2019 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time (9:00 a.m. Central). U.S. participants can dial (866) 342-8591 toll-free, while international participants can dial (203) 518-9713. The conference ID is GEOSQ319. A replay of the live call will be available for approximately 60 days. The company designs and manufactures seismic instruments and equipment, primarily marketed to the oil and gas industry for hydrocarbon reservoir monitoring. It also serves other industries with vibration monitoring, border security, and geotechnical applications. The company also produces non-seismic products such as water meters, imaging equipment, and offshore cables.

title: Navitas Systems Announces Dedicated New Building For Starlifter Lithium Material Handling Battery Production
summary: Navitas Systems announced the construction of a dedicated new building for Starlifter Lithium Material Handling Battery Production. The 100,000 square foot facility will expand annual capacity to 5,000 Starlifters and enable expansion of lithium cell production line. The new building is located near its existing 48,000 square foot Ann Arbor Michigan R&D and Manufacturing facility. The company reported nearly 200% year-over-year revenue growth in Starlifter sales. Kevin Hykin, President and COO, highlighted the expansion as a strategic move to support both commercial and government defense lithium cell businesses. Mil Ovan, President and CMO, noted a significant shift in the forklift market toward lithium batteries, especially in two and three shift applications. Navitas also secured the UL-ListedTM mark, becoming the only company offering 24, 36, and 48 volt lithium batteries with this accreditation.

title: Coal Baron Murray Stood Up for Miners Until He Ran Out of Money - Bloomberg
summary: Robert Murray, a prominent figure in the coal industry, has long been known for his support of union miners, a legacy that has become part of his story. However, his company, Murray Energy Corp, has faced significant financial challenges, leading to its bankruptcy filing. The company, which has been in operation for six decades, is now burdened with over $2.7 billion in debt. As part of a proposed restructuring, Murray, who is 79 years old, will no longer serve as the chief executive officer of the company he founded. A new entity will take over the company's assets, while the $8 billion in pension and health-care obligations to miners will be abandoned. This marks the end of an era for Murray, who has been a key player in the coal industry for many years.

summary: On May 31, 2013, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced new sanctions against Iran, targeting its petrochemical industry and efforts to evade sanctions. The actions were aimed at disrupting Iran's attempts to conceal oil transactions and support terrorism. The Treasury sanctioned Ferland Company Limited, a Cyprus and Ukraine-based company, for facilitating deceptive transactions for the National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC), which is a designated Iranian entity. These sanctions were implemented under Executive Order 13608, targeting foreign sanction evaders. The actions included designating companies involved in transactions with Iran's petrochemical sector and identifying several petrochemical companies as subject to sanctions due to their government control. The Treasury also targeted a scheme involving ship-to-ship oil transfers between three tankers, including the Blackstone, Zap, and Aldawha, which were part of a coordinated effort to evade sanctions. The Treasury identified Dimitris Cambis and his business network as working on behalf of Iran in March 2013. The U.S. Treasury Department announced new sanctions against Iran on May 31, 2013, as part of its ongoing efforts to curb Iran's illicit activities. The sanctions target Ferland under the Iran Sanctions Act (ISA), which prohibits visas for corporate officers, loans from U.S. financial institutions, and financial transactions under U.S. jurisdiction. Additionally, the Treasury identified eight Iranian petrochemical companies, including Bandar Imam Petrochemical Company and Pars Petrochemical Company, as being owned or controlled by the Iranian government. The Department also sanctioned two companies for engaging in significant transactions related to the purchase of petrochemical products from Iran. The sanctions also target aircraft procurement networks, including Kyrgyzstan-based Kyrgyz Trans Avia (KTA), Ukraine-based Ukrainian-Mediterranean Airlines (Um Air), and UAE-based Sirjanco Trading L.L.C., which are involved in leasing and selling aircraft to Mahan Air and Iran Air to circumvent U.S. sanctions. Mahan Air and Iran Air have been designated for providing support to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF) and other Iranian military entities. Officials from Um Air and KTA, as well as Mahan Air Managing Director Hamid Arabnejad, were also sanctioned. The Treasury identified additional aircraft operated by Mahan Air and Iran Air that have been blocked under E.O. 13224 and 13382.

title: Two federal programs helped expand police funding by over 200%
summary: Two federal programs, the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) and Byrne Justice Assistance Grants (Byrne JAG), have significantly expanded police funding in the United States. Between 1982 and 2015, federal spending on policing grew by 354%, outpacing both local and state spending. In 2015, local governments accounted for over two-thirds of police spending, while the federal government contributed 20.4%. The COPS program, established in 1994 under President Bill Clinton, provided $304 million in 2019 to law enforcement agencies. Byrne JAG, created in 1988 and consolidated in 2005, still averages around $435 million annually. Despite these increases, debates persist about the effectiveness of federal funding for law enforcement. Two federal programs helped expand police funding by over 200%. Some studies even suggested that the grants might not have been effective in cities with more than 250,000 people. In 2006, the Bush administration sought to eliminate all Byrne JAG funding due to a lack of demonstrable results, but it was eventually reauthorized through 2012. The movement to defund the police stems from the same question on whether communities benefit from millions of dollars in funding from federal, state and local governments. "People are recognizing that budgets often are related to power," says Rashawn Ray, a governance studies fellow at the Brookings Institution. "And in law enforcement, one of the things that we see is that the larger their budgets get, that hasn't necessarily correlated with a reduction in crime. So then people start saying, then why do their budgets look the way that it does?" Only time and more research will determine whether defunding the police will create safer communities. One thing that is for sure, the movement is leading to critical conversations at the local level on how to best protect citizens. "I think that this whole notion of defunding the police is an important conversation that's happening," said Ashton. "I think that we really need to think as a country about where we're investing in local, state and federal dollars, and how we're making the most use of that money to positively impact communities."

title: Federal Reserve Board - Agencies issue FAQ document regarding collateralized debt obligations backed by trust preferred securities under final rules implementing the "Volcker rule"
summary: On December 19, 2013, three U.S. federal financial institution regulatory agencies—the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency—issued a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) document to clarify guidance for banking entities regarding investments in 'Covered Funds' under the final rules implementing the Volcker Rule. The document addresses whether collateralized debt obligations (CDOs) backed by trust preferred securities (TruPS CDOs) qualify as Covered Funds. It clarifies that banks holding TruPS CDOs are not required to sell these holdings immediately but may use the conformance period, ending on July 21, 2015, to determine if they can be brought into compliance. The FAQs outline key legal considerations, including whether TruPS CDOs can be restructured to meet the final rules and whether a bank's investment constitutes an ownership interest. The final rules were approved on December 10, 2013.

Daniel emphasized the shift toward digital health technologies and AI, while Barsky highlighted the firm’s role in driving policy changes and connecting industry players. Walker noted the growing number of companies entering healthcare with new technologies to improve care quality and accessibility. The firm aims to provide strategic guidance to navigate complex regulatory environments and support innovation in value-based care.

title: Federal Reserve Board - Implementation Note issued September 18, 2019
summary: On September 18, 2019, the Federal Reserve Board issued an Implementation Note outlining decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). The Board of Governors voted unanimously to lower the interest rate paid on required and excess reserve balances to 1.80 percent, effective September 19, 2019. This rate was set 20 basis points below the top of the target range for the federal funds rate to foster trading within the FOMC's target range. The FOMC also authorized the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account, maintaining the federal funds rate in a target range of 1-3/4 to 2 percent. The Desk was directed to conduct overnight reverse repurchase operations at an offering rate of 1.70 percent, with reinvestment limits based on Treasury securities holdings and a $30 billion per day counterparty limit. Additionally, the Board approved a 1/4 percentage point decrease in the primary credit rate to 2.50 percent, effective September 19, 2019. The Federal Reserve Board issued an Implementation Note on September 18, 2019, outlining details regarding the implementation of monetary policy measures. This note was published on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website and reflects the latest updates as of that date. The document provides guidance on the operational aspects of policy decisions made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). It is important for market participants and financial institutions to review this note to understand the implications of recent policy actions. The note does not include any specific stock recommendations or financial forecasts, focusing instead on procedural and regulatory clarity.

summary: In June 2014, the average cost per hour worked for employee compensation among private industry employers varied significantly by major occupational group. For instance, in management, professional, and related occupations, employers spent an average of $53.52 per hour worked, with $37.20 for wages and salaries and $16.33 for benefits. In contrast, service occupations had employer costs of $14.10 per hour, with $10.72 for wages and salaries and $3.39 for benefits. Overall, employers spent an average of $30.11 per hour worked for employee compensation, with wages and salaries accounting for 69.8 percent of these costs and benefits making up the remaining 30.2 percent. These data are from the Employment Cost Trends program and are detailed in the report 'Employer Costs for Employee Compensation — June 2014'.

summary: IDEXX Laboratories, Inc. will begin selling its veterinary diagnostic merchandise products directly to U.S. veterinarians starting January 1, 2015, instead of through distributors. Henry Schein estimates that IDEXX product sales represent approximately $150 million in annualized revenue with mid-single digit margins. Selling IDEXX products is expected to contribute 4 to 6 cents to Henry Schein’s annual earnings per share, before offsetting other brand sales in 2015. Henry Schein stated that the change will have no impact on its 2014 results. The company also highlighted risks related to healthcare industry changes, regulatory compliance, data privacy, global operations, acquisitions, and litigation. It emphasized that these factors are not exhaustive and many are beyond its control.

title: Coronavirus devastates agriculture: Dumped milk, euthanized livestock
summary: The coronavirus pandemic has severely impacted the U.S. agriculture sector, leading to widespread issues such as dumped milk, euthanized livestock, and discarded crops. Long & Scott Farms, a Florida-based farm, faced a significant drop in demand for its cucumbers, which are typically used in restaurants. As a result, many of these cucumbers were discarded or left to rot in fields. Similarly, farmers in South Florida reported throwing away crops due to reduced demand in stores and restaurants. The situation has also affected livestock, with pork-processing plant closures leading to overcrowding in barns and discussions about euthanizing thousands of hogs. Tyson Foods, a major player in the industry, warned that plant closures would result in the loss of millions of animals. Dairy farmers, in particular, have been struggling with weak demand, with estimates suggesting up to 3.7 million gallons of milk are being dumped daily. The U.S. Agriculture Department has established a coordination center to assist livestock and poultry producers affected by these disruptions. Additionally, chicken processors have had to euthanize chickens due to staffing shortages and reduced processing capacity. Poultry farmers like Kerry and Barb Mergen in Albany, Minnesota, faced the difficult decision of euthanizing their flock due to the economic downturn caused by the virus. Only 15 hens managed to survive the process, highlighting the scale of the crisis. Meanwhile, mushroom farmer Matt Sicher in Lenhartsville, Pennsylvania, has lost revenue from restaurants in New York City, prompting a shift from wholesale to retail sales. The beef industry also suffered as slaughterhouse closures disrupted supply chains, with many meat-processing plants becoming virus hotspots. Despite these challenges, the U.S. government took steps to keep meat-processing plants operational through an executive order signed by President Trump. These events underscore the broader impact of the pandemic on food production and distribution.

summary: On September 21, 2017, Insperity, Inc. (NYSE: NSP) appointed Ellen Masterson to its Board of Directors. She was named a Class I director with an initial term expiring in 2020 and joined the Finance, Risk Management, and Audit Committee. Ms. Masterson received a pro rata share of the $105,000 Annual Director Award. No transactions under Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K were reported. Ellen Masterson, who retired as a partner with PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP in 2008, has also served as an independent director of Westwood Holdings Group (NYSE: WHG) and Westwood Trust since 2014. She chairs the audit committee of both entities and is a member of the WHG governance committee. Her expertise includes audits of financial services companies and public firms focused on mergers and acquisitions.

events.quote: Effective September 21, 2017, the Board of Directors of Insperity, Inc. (the “Company”) appointed Ellen Masterson to the Board of Directors.
Ms. Masterson will serve as a Class I director of the Company with an initial term expiring on the date of the Company’s annual meeting of stockholders in 2020.
Ms. Masterson has served as an independent director of Westwood Holdings Group (NYSE: WHG)
Ms. Masterson is the Chair of the audit committee of both WHG and Westwood Trust
Insperity delivers administrative relief, better benefits, reduced liabilities and a systematic way to improve productivity through its premier Workforce Optimization® solution.
Insperity business performance solutions support more than 100,000 businesses with over 2 million employees.
With 2016 revenues of $2.9 billion, Insperity operates in 61 offices throughout the United States.

title: The hot trend in smartphones? Not buying a new one
summary: The smartphone industry is facing a global slowdown in sales, with International Data Corporation reporting a 6.6% year-on-year decline in shipment volumes for the first quarter of 2019. To counter this, companies are introducing new, high-priced foldable devices and 5G-enabled phones. Samsung, the world's largest smartphone maker, launched the Galaxy Fold, a nearly $2,000 foldable smartphone that faced early issues. Huawei also announced a foldable phone priced around $2,600. However, consumer feedback from London, Singapore, and Guangzhou was largely negative, with users finding foldable phones strange and bulky. Ben Wood of CCS Insight noted that smartphones have become too similar in design and functionality, with marginal gains slowing down. Despite efforts to promote 5G technology, consumers remain hesitant to upgrade unless their current devices are no longer functional. The article discusses the growing interest in 5G technology and its potential impact on the smartphone market. While the United States is leading in 5G development, countries like China and Japan are also racing to launch their own versions of the technology. However, widespread adoption of 5G is expected to take time due to the ongoing construction of global infrastructure. Despite this, there is enthusiasm among potential customers for 5G phones. A user in Guangzhou expressed interest in purchasing a 5G phone because it is considered "trendy" and offers a "better internet system" that enables activities like video streaming. Similarly, a user in London mentioned that 5G would make tasks such as social media use and streaming Netflix more convenient. The article highlights the increasing demand for 5G technology and its potential to transform user experiences.

summary: Nordic American Tankers Ltd (NAT) secured a $306 million five-year senior secured credit agreement on February 12, 2019, arranged by CSG Investments, Inc., and funded by Beal Bank. The loan will retire its existing Revolving Credit Facility and reduce the effective interest rate compared to 2018. The loan amortizes over 20 years with full maturity after five years. NAT also leased three 2018 new buildings to settle major financial obligations. The company maintains low debt levels and aims to reduce them further. Its Suezmaxes market remains strong, and the recent plan supports future growth. Arctic Securities assisted in the transaction. NAT issued a cautionary statement on forward-looking statements, noting uncertainties and risks associated with future performance, including market conditions, charter rates, vessel values, and regulatory changes.

title: Will the American Dream still include owning a home?
summary: The article explores whether the American Dream still includes owning a home. Despite the housing crisis and mortgage crash, most Americans still desire home ownership. Fannie Mae's survey shows 70% of respondents would buy a home if they were moving, indicating the aspiration remains unchanged. HUD Secretary Shaun Donovan notes that the aspiration for home ownership is consistent, though the rules of funding have changed. Critics argue that the push for home ownership during the housing boom led to over-leveraging, and now underwriting is tighter. President Obama emphasized that hard work and responsibility should be rewarded through home ownership but warned against repeating past mistakes. Home ownership rates have declined from a peak of 69% to 65.2%. The article also discusses a proposed bill to dismantle Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, shifting mortgage finance to private investors. However, private investors remain cautious, limiting their involvement in the mortgage market. The article also highlights the growing single-family rental market, which has expanded from 10 million to 15 million homes, supported by institutional investors. Laurie Hawkes, president of American Residential Properties, argues that rental housing is becoming a preferred option for middle-class families and millennials, who value financial flexibility and job mobility. Fannie Mae's Duncan disputes this, stating that the stigma of renting has diminished, but the aspiration to own a home remains. He notes that younger generations are delaying home ownership due to longer education and career paths. The article also mentions that wealth creation is increasingly urban, with 80% of wealth generated in cities, as noted by MIT researchers. The future of home ownership may involve smaller units, co-ops, and services for seniors, adapting to changing societal needs.

summary: On April 20, 2016, Treasury Secretary Jacob J. Lew announced plans for the redesign of the U.S. $20, $10, and $5 notes. The new $20 bill will feature Harriet Tubman on its front, marking the first time a woman's portrait appears on U.S. currency in over a century. The reverse of the $10 note will depict the historic suffrage march ending at the Treasury Department, honoring leaders like Lucretia Mott and Susan B. Anthony. The $5 note will highlight events at the Lincoln Memorial and include figures such as Martin Luther King Jr. and Eleanor Roosevelt. The redesign aims to reflect the diversity of the nation and honor historical figures. The Bureau of Engraving and Printing will collaborate with the Federal Reserve to expedite the process, with the goal of releasing the new notes as quickly as possible while meeting security standards. The decision to feature Harriet Tubman on the new $20 was influenced by public feedback, particularly from children who viewed her as a role model. The new $10 will honor the women’s suffrage movement, including figures like Lucretia Mott and Susan B. Anthony, while the $5 will highlight events at the Lincoln Memorial, such as Marian Anderson’s 1939 performance and Martin Luther King Jr.’s 1963 speech. These redesigns aim to reflect the nation’s values and historical milestones.

summary: On February 11, 2014, Sangamo BioSciences, Inc. issued a press release announcing its financial results for the quarter and twelve months ended December 31, 2013. The company also announced that its 2014 Annual Meeting of Stockholders would be held on April 21, 2014, which is more than 30 days earlier than the anniversary date of the 2013 Annual Meeting. As a result, the deadline for stockholder nominations or proposals for consideration at the Annual Meeting set forth in the Company’s 2013 Proxy Statement no longer applies. Stockholders must submit their nominations or proposals by the close of business on February 21, 2014. This report from Sangamo BioSciences Inc. dated February 11, 2014, outlines the procedures for submitting proposals to the Annual Meeting. The company emphasizes that any stockholder wishing to present a proposal must provide notice by February 21, 2014, to ensure compliance with the Amended and Restated Bylaws and applicable regulations. The report also includes a press release issued on the same date and is signed by Edward O. Lanphier II, the President and Chief Executive Officer. The document is filed as an exhibit to the Current Report on Form 8-K.

title: Gertler Earns Billions in Mine Deals as Congo Remains Poorest - Bloomberg
summary: Dan Gertler, an Israeli billionaire, has amassed significant wealth through his investments in mining and other sectors in the Democratic Republic of Congo. His journey began in 1997 when he arrived in the country seeking rough diamonds. Over the years, Gertler has expanded his portfolio to include iron ore, gold, cobalt, and copper, as well as agriculture, oil, and banking. His latest project, the Musonoie-T17 copper and cobalt mine operated by Katanga Mining Ltd., is a massive installation twice the size of Monaco. This mine transforms ore mined from the ochre earth into sheets of copper, showcasing Gertler's continued success in the mining industry despite the country's status as one of the poorest in the world.

title: State of American farming: Big producers dominate food production
summary: The State of American farming is undergoing significant changes, as highlighted by the recently released agriculture census. U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Tom Vilsack warned of an 'eroding middle' in farming, noting that a small number of large farm operations produce the vast majority of the nation's food. According to the census, large farms with over $1 million in sales account for only 4 percent of all farms but generate 66 percent of all sales. In contrast, three quarters of U.S. farms gross only $50,000 a year and account for only 4 percent of product sales. Darren Hudson, a professor at Texas Tech University, explained that smaller farms are often 'hobby' farms with significant off-farm income, and their small output is not a problem. Justin Gardner, a professor at Middle Tennessee State University, noted that the census dispels the misconception that most farms are large corporations, as many are large family farms that formed corporations for benefits. The census also found that 30 percent of all farm operators are women, and the number of Latino farm operators has increased by 21 percent since 2007. Sales of organically farmed food have increased by 82 percent to $3.1 billion in 2012, and direct sales from farms to consumers have risen by 8.1 percent to over $1.3 billion. California leads in agriculture sales, with Fresno County ranking first with nearly $5 billion in sales. The average age of farmers has increased to 58.3 years, but there is a 11.3 percent increase in young, beginning principal operators, indicating a potential change in the industry. As of 2014, there were approximately 3.2 million farmers operating 2.1 million farms across 914.5 million acres of farmland in the United States. In 2012, both sales and production expenses reached record highs, with U.S. producers selling $394.6 billion worth of agricultural products and spending $328.9 billion to produce them. USDA Secretary Tom Vilsack emphasized the need to support smaller farms by creating new market opportunities and providing access to capital, credit, and disaster assistance. A notable positive trend was the increase in farms with Internet access, which rose to 69.6 percent in 2012 from 56.5 percent in 2007. Gardner from Middle Tennessee State noted that this trend is exciting as it allows farmers to improve their production and marketing through the Internet.

summary: On July 9, 2018, HENRY SCHEIN INC reported in its 8-K filing that it is currently unable to estimate the amount or range of costs expected to be incurred in connection with certain activities. The company stated it will file an amendment to the Current Report on Form 8-K once it determines such estimates. The filing was signed by Walter Siegel, Senior Vice President and General Counsel. The Company also committed to an initiative to rationalize its operations and provide expense efficiencies, with these activities expected to be complete by the end of 2018.

summary: Royal Bank of Canada announced on January 29, 2014, that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Jamaican banking operations, including RBC Royal Bank (Jamaica) Limited and RBTT Securities Jamaica Limited, to Sagicor Group Jamaica Limited. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals, and is expected to be finalized in the coming months. The move aligns with RBC's strategy to focus on regions with significant market share while repositioning its Caribbean business. The deal is expected to result in an estimated loss of C$60 million (before and after-tax) due to International Financial Reporting Standards, primarily from a writedown of goodwill and intangibles acquired in 2008. The loss will be reflected in the first quarter 2014 results, with results and an earnings call scheduled for February 26, 2014.

events.quote: Royal Bank of Canada (RY on TSX and NYSE) today announced that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell RBC Royal Bank (Jamaica) Limited and RBTT Securities Jamaica Limit
RBC expects the transaction to result in an estimated loss of C$60 million (before and after-tax) as a result of International Financial Reporting Standards
The transaction is not expected to have a material impact on RBCs Basel III Common Equity Tier 1 ratio
RBC will release its first quarter 2014 results and host an earnings conference call on February 26, 2014

summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury has issued a call for Large Position Reports from entities holding positions in the 2-1/4% Treasury Notes of November 2027. Entities with positions equal to or exceeding $4.58 billion as of January 12, 2018, are required to report these positions to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Reports must be submitted by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on April 16, 2018. The reporting threshold is $4.58 billion in par value, and the maturity date of the notes is November 15, 2027. The call for reports is based on Treasury's large position reporting rules (17 CFR Part 420).

title: Coca-Cola (KO) earnings Q3 2019: Revenue beats expectations
summary: Coca-Cola (KO) reported third-quarter 2019 earnings that exceeded analysts' expectations, with revenue reaching $9.5 billion, surpassing the $9.4 billion forecast. The company's earnings per share (EPS) came in at 56 cents, matching the 56 cents expected. CEO James Quincey highlighted the success of the Coke Zero Sugar line and smaller can sizes, which drove sales growth. Organic revenue grew by 5%, supported by higher prices and increased demand for premium drinks. Despite declining soda consumption in the U.S., Coca-Cola has focused on healthier options and smaller packaging to boost sales. The company also plans to address weaker performance in its water brands by exploring more sustainable packaging solutions, such as aluminum cans for Dasani. Coca-Cola Plus Coffee and Coke Energy are expanding globally, with the latter set to debut in the U.S. in January. Quincey noted that Brexit-related concerns in the U.K. have impacted business sentiment, but he remains optimistic about potential improvements if the Brexit deal is finalized. Coca-Cola updated its 2019 organic revenue growth outlook to at least 5%, and provided a partial forecast for fiscal 2020, anticipating currency headwinds of 1% to 2% for revenue and 2% to 3% for operating income.

title: Infineon to buy International Rectifier for $3B
summary: Infineon Technologies, a German semiconductor company, announced on August 20, 2014, that it would acquire U.S.-based semiconductor firm International Rectifier for approximately $3 billion in cash. The deal, valued at $40 per share, represents a 48% premium over the average share price for the past three months and a 51% premium over Tuesday's closing price. The acquisition is expected to enhance Infineon's strategic development by integrating International Rectifier's expertise in customer needs and application understanding. Infineon plans to fund the transaction using its cash reserves and credit facilities totaling 1.5 billion euros ($2.0 billion). The move follows shareholder pressure on CEO Reinhard Ploss to utilize Infineon's cash reserves for acquisitions or returns to investors.

summary: Murray Energy, a major U.S. coal mining company, has emerged from federal bankruptcy protection under a new name and ownership group. The company's Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan was approved in U.S. bankruptcy court in Ohio and became effective on September 16, 2020. Murray Energy Holdings completed the sale of its assets to an entity formed by former creditors, and the new company, American Consolidated Natural Resources Inc. (ACNR), is now the largest privately owned U.S. coal operator. ACNR operates active mines in Alabama, Kentucky, Ohio, West Virginia, and Utah, and has management services agreements to operate Foresight Energy mines in Illinois and Murray Energy subsidiary Murray Metallurgical mines. The restructuring eliminated over $8 billion in debt and legacy liabilities, providing ACNR with enhanced financial flexibility. Robert Moore, who replaced Robert Murray as CEO in 2019, now leads the new company, which has over 4,000 employees. The bankruptcy filing marked a significant political failure for President Donald Trump, who had sought to end what he called a 'war on coal' by Democrats. ACNR has also hired members of the United Mine Workers union, who formerly worked at Murray Energy.

summary: The State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) is a U.S. government program aimed at supporting small businesses through credit support and investment programs. The initiative was funded by the American Rescue Plan Act, signed into law on March 11, 2021, which allocated $10 billion to support state, territory, and Tribal government programs. The SSBCI program focuses on catalyzing investment in underserved entrepreneurs and venture capital fund managers. The Treasury Department has released various resources, including a guidebook on communications and media relations, and has launched an application portal for the Technical Assistance Grant Program. The program has also undergone several deadline extensions for tribal governments and states, with the latest updates as of 2022. The initiative is part of broader efforts to support small business growth and economic recovery. The U.S. Department of the Treasury has been actively involved in supporting small businesses through the State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI), which aims to provide financing and technical assistance to small businesses, particularly in underserved communities. The initiative has supported over $3.1 billion in new financing for small businesses, with additional funding allocated to tribal governments and states. The Treasury has also announced new funding for small businesses in various states and territories as part of the Biden-Harris Administration’s Investing in America Agenda. These efforts include technical assistance programs and funding for historically underserved entrepreneurs. The SSBCI has been a key part of the administration’s strategy to drive economic growth and support small business success across the United States. The U.S. Department of the Treasury has been actively supporting small business growth and entrepreneurship through the State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI) as part of the Biden administration's Investing in America agenda. The initiative has allocated significant funds to various states, territories, and tribal governments to promote economic development and support underserved entrepreneurs. For instance, up to $353.4 million was approved for four states, and $339 million for three states and two U.S. territories. Additionally, Puerto Rico received up to $109 million to foster small business growth. The initiative also includes technical assistance programs, such as deploying $300 million in support for underserved entrepreneurs and very small businesses. The timeline includes key events like the release of the SSBCI Investing in America Small Business Opportunity Program (SBOP) NOFO and a pre-application webinar scheduled for November 6, 2023. The U.S. Department of the Treasury implemented the Social Security Benefits and Community Investment (SSBCI) program as part of the American Rescue Plan Act signed by President Biden on March 11, 2021. The program aimed to provide financial assistance to Tribal Governments, states, territories, and municipalities. Key dates included a Tribal Consultation on May 27, 2021, with responses due for the request for information on June 4, 2021. Preliminary allocation amounts were provided to Tribal governments by June 30, 2021. Applications for SSBCI capital programs from states, territories, and Washington, DC were initiated by December 11, 2021, and completed by February 11, 2022. Municipalities in states not applying for SSBCI had to submit applications by March 11, 2022. Technical assistance funding applications were due by October 14, 2022, and Tribal governments had to complete their applications by October 31, 2022. The comment deadline for the RFI was extended to November 3, 2022, allowing stakeholders to submit feedback on Regulations.gov.

summary: Strauss Group (TASE: STRS), an Israeli-based food and beverage company, is hosting one of the biggest food-tech events of the year, FoodTechIL 2019, which will take place next week in Hanger 11, Tel Aviv Port. The event will host over 1,200 participants from around the world, including senior executives from major Food & Beverage companies such as PepsiCo, Danone, Mondelez, and Jivaudan. Over 50 international startup companies will also exhibit, showcasing the most innovative and breakthrough technologies in food-tech. The event will begin at 8:30 AM and will include a main plenary session and six round table "foodtalks" in partnerships with food and beverage companies, covering topics such as plastics, the future of protein, food & health, circular food, and more. Strauss Group has invested in food tech innovation through the kitchen food tech hub and the formation of Alpha Strauss eight years ago, with a vision to leverage technologies and enable the company to accelerate global growth and provide solutions for major challenges in the food chain value. The startup companies attending the event are working in various fields of the industry, including alternative ingredients, health & wellness, food safety, production systems, and food chain. Ofra Strauss, Chairperson of Strauss Group, emphasized the crucial role of businesses in using technology to make a positive impact on society, people's health, and the environment. Giora BarDea, CEO & President of Strauss Group, highlighted the importance of thinking ahead to stay ahead and preparing for the consumer of the future, noting that Israel is rapidly evolving from the startup nation to the FoodTech nation.
