title: How Top Funds Are Trading America’s Superpower Clash With China
summary: The U.S.-China relationship is deteriorating, and top funds are adjusting their strategies to navigate the ongoing superpower clash. Investment managers like Mark Mobius and Andy Rothman are analyzing the implications for investors. Mobius, with over four decades of experience in emerging markets, believes the U.S.-China dissonance is long-term and not likely to improve soon. He emphasizes the importance of focusing on Chinese companies that are not directly impacted by trade tensions, such as those in healthcare and education. Rothman highlights the shift in the Chinese economy toward domestic demand rather than manufacturing or exports. These insights reflect the broader industry trend of adapting investment strategies to the evolving geopolitical landscape. Matthews China Fund has outperformed 87% of peers in the past five years. Most people are unaware that the Chinese economy has evolved into one that is driven by domestic demand, and not by manufacturing or exports. Almost every Chinese company we invest in is a domestic company selling goods and services to local consumers. So this worsening of relations won’t affect them. A few years ago, we looked carefully at our holdings in China that might have been affected by tariffs applied by Trump and made adjustments to that. So we are constantly evolving at a stock level. Now with discussions about transfer of U.S. technology or intellectual property to Chinese companies, we have already gone through and scrubbed our holdings to avoid that. For the moment, prospects are better for Chinese companies oriented toward internal growth. While there are risks for companies relying heavily on U.S. IP or technology, there are also opportunities in Chinese technology companies that are trying to be an alternative source for IP and equipment. My assumption is that the political relationship is going to continue to deteriorate between now and November. It seems to be part of president Trump’s re-election strategy. At the same time, I don’t think it is going to descend into chaos or conflict. Kelvin Tay, Singapore-based Asia Pacific chief investment officer at UBS Global Wealth Management, which oversaw $2.6 trillion as of the end of July. Within Asia ex-Japan equities, we are neutral on some markets including China. We have China on a neutral rating because of the fact that we thought that rhetoric will increase about two months back and rightly so, it actually increased. We think that the noise will get increasingly louder in the next couple of months. The Chinese equity market has done really well. It’s time to do a little bit more of a rotation, and I would re-balance my Chinese equity exposure into Asian high yield and the Chinese yuan relative to the dollar. In Asian high yield, basically 60% is Chinese high yield. So you’re still exposed to China but in a different asset class. This is where we think a lot of the upside is. If the Democrats take over then we can expect a lot more nuanced foreign policy vis-a-vis the one the Trump administration has. When you’re dealing with a civilization and not just a country, you need to be a lot more sophisticated with regards to your foreign policy and that’s not something the current administration has been able to demonstrate.

title: GE to break up into 3 companies focusing on aviation, health care and energy
summary: General Electric (GE) announced plans to split into three separate companies, each focusing on aviation, health care, and energy. The decision, made public on November 9, 2021, aims to enhance focus, capital allocation, and strategic flexibility for each unit. The health-care unit is set to be spun off by early 2023, while the energy unit will follow by early 2024. GE shares rose over 2% on the day of the announcement, despite a broader market pullback. CEO Lawrence Culp emphasized the benefits of creating industry-leading public companies, stating that the move would allow each unit to better serve customers and investors. The company has been struggling with underperformance over the past two decades, losing 2% annually since 2009 compared to the S&P 500's 9% return. The spinoffs are expected to incur about $2 billion in transaction and operational costs, with the energy segment anticipated to have the least debt. GE plans to use proceeds from the recent sale of its aviation financing unit to reduce its debt, which is expected to total less than $65 billion by the end of 2021.

summary: The U.S. Treasury Department announced the release of the 2016 U.S. Model Income Tax Treaty on February 17, 2016. This treaty serves as the baseline text used in negotiating tax treaties. The 2016 Model includes provisions aimed at eliminating double taxation without creating opportunities for non-taxation or reduced taxation through tax evasion or avoidance. It also addresses corporate inversions by denying reduced withholding taxes on U.S. source payments made by companies that engage in inversions. The Treasury Department emphasized the importance of resolving disputes between tax authorities through mandatory binding arbitration, aligning with existing U.S. tax treaties. The 2016 Model reflects feedback from comments received on the proposed model treaty provisions released in May 2015. The U.S. Treasury Department has announced the release of the 2016 U.S. Model Income Tax Treaty, which includes a detailed technical explanation. This explanation is intended to address certain situations related to the 'active trade or business' test under Article 22 (Limitation on Benefits). The Treasury plans to release this technical explanation this spring. The preamble to the 2016 Model invites public comments on these situations, and the deadline for submitting feedback is April 18, 2016. The public can access the 2016 Model and its accompanying preamble for further details.

title: GigOptix Reports Record Third Quarter Fiscal 2012 Financial Results
summary: GigOptix, Inc. (NYSE MKT: GIG) reported record third quarter fiscal 2012 financial results, with total revenue increasing 20% to $10.1 million from $8.4 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2011. The company also saw a 5% increase from $9.6 million in the second quarter of fiscal 2012. Non-GAAP net income for the quarter was $0.02 per diluted share, compared to a net loss of $0.03 per share in the same period of fiscal 2011. Cash and cash equivalents at the end of the quarter were $12.3 million. The company highlighted its growth in key areas, including its optics product line and RF/MMIC business, driven by increased market interest in its E-band offerings. GigOptix reported record third quarter fiscal 2012 financial results, highlighting its ongoing legal battle against former employees and Optomai, Inc. The company is actively prosecuting a lawsuit for misappropriation of confidential information and trade secrets, having gathered substantial evidence through forensic work. GigOptix is moving the case toward trial, with Dr. Katz expressing confidence in the evidence. Financially, the company noted progress in market penetration and customer adoption of new products, but warned of increased macroeconomic uncertainty and short lead times in high-speed optical communications markets. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue to be in line with the third quarter due to cautious outlook. GigOptix will host a conference call and webcast to discuss the results and business outlook.

title: TSMC to Spend at Least $40 Billion to Address Chip Shortage
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. raised its growth projections and unveiled record spending plans for 2022, signaling that the voracious demand for chips that has fueled a months-long supply chain squeeze will persist for years. The company foresees sales of $16.6 billion to $17.2 billion in the first quarter alone, at least 5% ahead of estimates. It intends to spend $40 billion to $44 billion expanding and upgrading capacity in 2022.

summary: On March 17, 2015, Medallion Financial Corp purchased 45,000 shares of common stock at $10.16 per share, totaling $457,184. As of March 17, 2015, $13,662,859 remains available for future stock repurchases under the Current Stock Repurchase Program. On July 29, 2014, the Board of Directors authorized management to repurchase up to $20,000,000 of the Company’s common stock. Since November 2003, the company has repurchased 2,221,876 shares at an average cost of $9.29 per share.

events.quote: On March 17, 2015, the Company purchased a total of 45,000 shares of common stock at a cost of $457,184, or $10.16 per share, inclusive of brokerage commissions and fees.
As of March 17, 2015, $13,662,859 remains available for future stock repurchases under the Current Stock Repurchase Program.

summary: On February 1, 2012, Blonder Tongue Laboratories, Inc.'s subsidiary, R. L. Drake Holdings, LLC, entered into an asset purchase agreement with R. L. Drake, LLC, R. L. Drake Acquisition Corporation, and WBMK Holding Company. The agreement involved the acquisition of substantially all of R. L. Drake, LLC's assets, including manufacturing equipment, inventory, receivables, and intellectual property related to electronic communications solutions for cable television systems, digital television reception, and video signal distribution. The purchase price was approximately $6,476,995, subject to adjustments, plus contingent payments of up to $1,500,000 over three years if certain financial results are achieved. The acquisition includes indemnification obligations and a five-year non-compete clause for the seller and its members. The company issued a press release on February 2, 2012, announcing the acquisition, which is attached as Exhibit 99.1. Financial statements and pro forma information are not included in the report but are intended to be filed by amendment within 71 calendar days. The acquisition is expected to impact the company's operations and industry position.

summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. (TSX: BAM.A) (Euronext: BAMA) closed the sale of Longview Timber and Longview Fibre Paper and Packaging for aggregate proceeds of $3.675 billion. Longview Timber was sold to Weyerhaeuser Co. for $2.65 billion, yielding net cash proceeds of approximately $600 million. Longview Fibre Paper and Packaging was sold to KapStone Paper and Packaging for $1.025 billion, yielding net cash proceeds of approximately $250 million. The closing of these two transactions increased Brookfield’s liquidity by approximately $850 million and resulted in an attractive risk-adjusted return on capital to Brookfield, its flagship public infrastructure entity and investors in Brookfield’s private funds.

events.quote: Brookfield sold Longview Timber to Weyerhaeuser Co. for $2.65 billion.
Brookfield closed the sale of Longview Fibre Paper and Packaging to KapStone Paper and Packaging for $1.025 billion.
The closing of these two transactions increased Brookfield’s liquidity by approximately $850 million and resulted in an attractive risk-adjusted return on capital to Brookfield,

summary: Brown Gibbons Lang & Company (BGL) released a report highlighting LED lighting's transformative impact on the industry. LED technology is driving rapid market penetration due to energy savings, longer life, and improving light quality. M&A activity remains high as companies leverage acquisitions to build scale and adopt intelligent lighting solutions. In May, Philips announced plans to sell at least 25% of its Lighting Division via IPO. Acuity Brands acquired Juno Lighting for $385 million at a 12.0x EBITDA multiple. Private equity firms have also shown interest, with several notable platform acquisitions. BGL, an independent investment bank, provides M&A advisory and capital raising services across multiple sectors. The report underscores the growing demand for connected lighting systems and the convergence of LED lighting with controls to enable integrated networks.

summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. announced the final close of Brookfield Strategic Real Estate Partners II (BSREP II) with US$9.0 billion in equity commitments, exceeding the original US$7.0 billion target. The Fund will invest in high-quality property assets across North America, Europe, Australia, Brazil, and other select markets. Brookfield has committed US$2.3 billion to the Fund, aligning its interests with investors. To date, the Fund has committed over $4.0 billion in investments in the U.S., Europe, and Brazil. Brian Kingston, CEO of Brookfield Property Group, stated that the fundraise exceeded the target, showing continued demand for real estate investment with a strong global sponsor. The Fund is already 45% committed, and there are attractive opportunities to deploy capital globally.

title: Life Insurance Customer Satisfaction Flatlines Despite Pandemic Fears, J.D. Power Finds
summary: Despite the pandemic's impact, J.D. Power's latest findings indicate that customer satisfaction with life insurance remains flat. The report highlights that even as deaths related to COVID-19 surpass 200,000 in the United States, consumer interest in purchasing life insurance has not significantly increased. This suggests that while the pandemic has raised awareness of mortality risks, it has not translated into a surge in life insurance purchases. The data underscores a potential disconnect between public health concerns and consumer behavior in the insurance sector. J.D. Power's analysis provides insight into how insurers might need to adapt their strategies to better align with customer expectations during these uncertain times.

summary: Insperity, Inc. amended its credit agreement with ZB, N.A. dba Amegy Bank on February 6, 2018, increasing the revolving credit facility to $350 million with an option to raise it to $400 million. The swing line loan and letter of credit subfacilities were raised to $30 million each. The agreement, which matures on February 6, 2023, is secured by 65% of the stock of the company’s captive insurance subsidiary and guaranteed by all domestic subsidiaries. Interest rates depend on the leverage ratio, with margins ranging from 1.50% to 2.25% for LIBOR loans and 0.00% to 0.50% for alternate base rate loans. The alternate base rate is defined as the highest of the prime rate, federal funds rate plus 0.50%, or the bank’s prime rate. The agreement includes financial covenants limiting the company’s minimum interest coverage ratio and maximum leverage ratio. The document was referenced in Exhibit 10.1 to the Form 8-K filing and included in the press release issued on February 12, 2018, signed by Daniel D. Herink, Senior Vice President of Legal, General Counsel and Secretary.

summary: The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. issued a press release announcing its financial results for the fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2019. The release includes the Company’s estimates related to its fiscal 2020 second half and full year net sales and diluted net earnings per common share. On February 5, 2020, the Company declared a quarterly dividend in the amount of $.48 per share on the Company’s Class A and Class B Common Stock. The dividend is payable in cash on March 16, 2020 to stockholders of record at the close of business on February 28, 2020. A copy of the press release is attached hereto as Exhibit 99.1 and is incorporated herein by reference.

title: Ocean Link, the First Private Equity Firm Focused on China's Travel and Tourism Sector, Announces Strategic Partnership with Ctrip and General Atlantic
summary: Ocean Link, a private equity firm focused on China's travel and tourism sector, has announced a strategic partnership with Ctrip and General Atlantic. The collaboration aims to leverage Ocean Link's expertise in the travel and tourism industry to support growth opportunities. Ctrip.com International, Ltd. is a leading travel service provider in China, offering accommodation reservation, transportation ticketing, and corporate travel management services. General Atlantic, established in 1980, combines a collaborative global approach, sector-specific expertise, long-term investment horizon, and a deep understanding of growth drivers to partner with great management and build exceptional businesses worldwide. The partnership is positioned to capitalize on the steady growth of China's travel and tourism sector, which has seen significant increases in domestic and international travel numbers over the past decade.

title: Why transportation networks are especially vulnerable to ransomware
summary: Transportation networks are especially vulnerable to ransomware attacks due to the high susceptibility of workers to phishing emails. A ransomware attack on San Francisco's light rail system over the Thanksgiving weekend highlighted the impact cybercriminals can have on municipal transportation systems. The attack occurred because a worker invited hackers in by clicking on a malicious link or email attachment, which can quickly spread the virus if the network is interconnected. Ransomware is expected to be a $1 billion cybercriminal business in 2016, according to the FBI. PhishMe's 2016 report found that transportation workers were more likely to open phishing emails than workers in other industries, with about 22% falling for the test scenario. Education workers had the highest susceptibility at 28%, while the average across all industries was 17%. The FBI recommends not paying the ransom, as the San Francisco agency was able to do due to its system backups. Many organizations, especially underfunded government agencies, are not well-prepared for such attacks. PhishMe CEO Rohyt Belani emphasized the importance of frequent backups, updated security software, and employee training to detect suspicious emails. Transportation networks are especially vulnerable to ransomware due to the increasing integration of internet-connected devices. Cybersecurity experts warn that as more devices become part of the internet of things, ransomware attacks could target critical infrastructure such as vehicles and medical devices like pacemakers. Ben Johnson, chief security strategist at Carbon Black, highlights the merging of physical and cyber security, emphasizing that when human safety is at risk, there is greater public awareness and response. This convergence underscores the growing threat of ransomware in the transportation sector and beyond.

title: Sears appoints board member with restructuring experience
summary: Sears Holdings added restructuring expert Alan Carr to its board as it faces a key debt payment it may not meet. Carr, CEO of restructuring advisory firm Drivetrain, previously served as director of reorganized businesses. Sears CEO Eddie Lampert welcomed Carr, stating his expertise would help maximize value for the company and stakeholders. Sears shares fell 1.5% premarket, trading at 63 cents, below $1 for the first time. A special committee is evaluating Lampert's proposal to buy assets through his hedge fund ESL Investments, which could reduce Sears' debt by nearly 80% to $1.24 billion. Debtholders must be convinced Sears is worth more than its assets, despite constant losses. The longer Sears delays bankruptcy, the more its asset value may decline. Lampert owns about 31% of Sears' shares, giving him control over the company's fate.

title: TradeStation und TradingView verkünden API-Integration
summary: TradeStation Securities Inc. (ein Unternehmen der Monex-Gruppe und preisgekrönter Online-Broker u.a. für Futures-Kommissionshandel) wird im dritten Quartal 2019 in das TradingPanel von TradingView integriert. Die strategische Zusammenarbeit ermöglicht bestehenden TradingView-Usern, Trading-Orders aufzugeben und von der robusten Orderausführung von TradeStation zu profitieren. Neue TradeStation-Handelskonten, einschließlich solcher, die von TradingView-Usern eröffnet und bis zum 31. August 2019 kapitalisiert werden, erhalten bis 2020 provisionsfreien Handel.

summary: On September 23, 2020, Blonder Tongue Laboratories, Inc. (NYSE American: BDR) received a U.S. patent for its NXG video delivery platform. The patent, US10,785,829, covers technologies within the NeXgen Gateway (NXG) platform, which is used by telecommunications, cable television, and IP television service providers to deliver data, video, and audio content to residential and enterprise locations. The ’829 patented technology is anticipated to ease migration from traditional video delivery architectures, transmission and signal protection technologies, into modern IP-based digital content protection transmission and delivery designs. The NXG platform can also help service providers more securely monitor and maintain those systems prior to, during and following their IP television migration projects, and its fully modular design helps operators adapt their content delivery requirements over time without the need to fork-lift upgrade their video transmission infrastructure in the future.

summary: On January 25, 2021, Nicholas Financial, Inc. announced the opening of a new branch office in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The company issued a press release detailing the expansion, which is part of its strategy to increase its market presence. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 to the Form 8-K filing. This event is reported under Item 8.01 of the Form 8-K, indicating it is an 'Other Events' disclosure. The information provided is not deemed 'filed' under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, nor is it incorporated by reference into any other filing unless explicitly stated. The expansion is a strategic move to enhance the company's operations in the region.

summary: Impac Mortgage Holdings Inc announced the cancellation of the Special Meeting of its Series B Preferred Stockholders, originally scheduled for September 13, 2018. The decision followed a court ruling on September 5, 2018, where the Circuit Court for Baltimore City granted a stay pending the conclusion of the appeal of a July 16, 2018 Judgement Order. The order required the company to hold a special meeting to elect directors. The company had previously filed an appeal of the Judgement Order. The cancellation of the meeting reflects the ongoing legal proceedings and the company's appeal process.

title: Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement of longer-run goals and policy strategy
summary: On January 25, 2012, the Federal Reserve issued a FOMC statement outlining its longer-run goals and policy strategy. The statement emphasized that inflation over the longer run is primarily determined by monetary policy. The Committee judged that inflation at a rate of 2 percent, as measured by the annual change in the price index for personal consumption expenditures, is most consistent with the Federal Reserve's statutory mandate. The goal is to keep longer-term inflation expectations firmly anchored, fostering price stability and moderate long-term interest rates. The maximum level of employment is largely determined by nonmonetary factors affecting the labor market. The Committee does not specify a fixed goal for employment, instead relying on assessments of maximum employment levels. FOMC participants' estimates of the longer-run normal rate of unemployment had a central tendency of 5.2 percent to 6.0 percent, unchanged from last January but higher than several years earlier. The Committee seeks to mitigate deviations of inflation from its longer-run goal and deviations of employment from its assessments of maximum levels.

summary: Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation completed the purchase of 7,475,537 ordinary shares of Faiveley Transport, representing approximately 51% of its outstanding share capital, under the Share Purchase Agreement dated October 6, 2015. The transaction involved approximately $212 million in cash and 6.3 million shares of WAB common stock. Wabtec France will file a mandatory tender offer to acquire the remaining shares of Faiveley Transport, with the total purchase price expected to reach approximately $1.7 billion, including assumed debt. The common stock used as consideration was issued under Section 4(a)(2) and/or Regulation S of the Securities Act of 1933. The acquisition led to the election of Philippe Alfroid and Erwan Faiveley to the Board of Directors of WAB on November 30, 2016, as per the Shareholders Agreement. The transaction is subject to the terms and conditions of the Tender Offer Agreement dated October 6, 2015, as amended.

summary: On July 1, 2020, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced its intention to provide a $700 million loan to YRC Worldwide Inc. The loan was part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (CARES Act), and the Treasury had reached an agreement with YRC on June 30, 2020, to receive a 29.6% equity stake in the company. The decision was based on a certification by the Secretary of Defense that YRC is critical to maintaining national security. YRC provides 68% of less-than-truckload services to the Department of Defense and is a leading provider of critical military transportation and other hauling services to the U.S. government. The loan will help YRC maintain approximately 30,000 trucking jobs and continue to support essential military supply chain operations and the transport of industrial, commercial, and retail goods to more than 200,000 corporate customers across North America. The Treasury intends to provide loans totaling $700 million, maturing on September 30, 2024, and will receive shares totaling 29.6% of YRC’s common stock on a fully diluted basis, to be held in a voting trust. The agreement will also include provisions to maintain employment levels and limit executive compensation, dividends, and share repurchases.

title: BEA is Launching the Survey of New Foreign Direct Investment (BE-13)!
summary: The U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) launched the Survey of New Foreign Direct Investment (BE-13) on November 21, 2014. The survey collects data on new investments made by foreign investors establishing, acquiring, or expanding U.S. businesses. This data will help assess the impact of foreign direct investment on the U.S. economy, advise foreign investors, and support national and state policies to attract such investments. Entities subject to BE-13 reporting requirements must respond, regardless of whether they are contacted by BEA.

title: Distressed Denim: Levi’s Tries to Adapt to the Yoga Pants Era
summary: Levi Strauss, the company that invented jeans, is now trying to adapt to the rise of yoga pants. The brand, which has survived major historical events like the Civil War and the Great Depression, is now facing a new challenge: the popularity of yoga pants, which have started to outsell jeans in the U.S. According to market researcher NPD Group, athletic pants sold in about equal numbers to jeans for the first time in the U.S., as revenue from women’s jeans fell 8 percent. At Levi’s, the yoga pants trend is especially problematic, disrupting a turnaround plan led by the new CEO. Bart Sights, Levi’s senior director for technical innovation, is working to create women’s skinny jeans that have the right amount of stretch without losing their denim essence. His team is experimenting with techniques like contouring, using lasers to etch away the top layer of indigo to create a slimmer look. They are also developing new materials to ensure comfort without compromising the traditional feel of denim. For Levi’s, innovation is a delicate balance between modern comfort and the 19th-century essence of jeans. Levi’s, once a dominant force in the denim market, faced declining sales as traditional jeans lost appeal to younger consumers. Sales dropped from $10 billion to $4.8 billion, partly due to the decline of large department stores. The company, privately owned by its founder’s heirs, was slow to adapt to changing consumer preferences. In 2011, Chip Bergh became CEO, aiming to reinvent the brand. He emphasized innovation, customer engagement, and expanding into women’s jeans, which accounted for only 23% of Levi’s business. However, Levi’s struggled to compete with brands like Lululemon, which popularized yoga pants as a versatile, stylish alternative. Levi’s misread the shift toward stretchy, functional denim, leading to a loss of market share. Analysts criticized the company for ignoring customer preferences and failing to innovate. Bergh’s efforts to revamp the brand included restructuring, cost-cutting, and rethinking product lines, but the challenge of adapting to the ‘yoga pants era’ remained significant.

summary: TG Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: TGTX) presented long-term follow-up data from the Phase 2 and Open Label Extension (OLE) trial of ublituximab (TG-1101), its novel glycoengineered anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, in relapsing forms of Multiple Sclerosis (RMS) at the American Academy of Neurology 71st Annual Meeting on May 7, 2019. The data showed that ublituximab is well tolerated with a median follow-up of 97.5 weeks. No patients discontinued treatment due to drug-related adverse events. AEs were infrequent during the OLE, with only 4 patients (9%) experiencing infusion-related reactions (IRRs), all Grade 1 or 2. The data support the ongoing Phase 3 ULTIMATE program, which is fully enrolled and expected to report results next year. TG Therapeutics is also developing umbralisib (TGR-1202) and other therapies for hematological malignancies and autoimmune diseases.

summary: Schweitzer-Mauduit International, Inc. issued a press release on February 1, 2012, announcing its earnings for the quarter ended December 31, 2011. The earnings release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 to the Form 8-K filing. The report is not considered 'filed' under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, nor is it incorporated by reference in any filing under the Securities Act of 1933 or the Exchange Act, except as expressly set forth by specific reference to such filings. The press release provides details about the company's financial performance for the quarter, which is relevant to its operations and financial condition. The filing includes the press release as an exhibit and is signed by Mark A. Spears, the Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer of Schweitzer-Mauduit International, Inc.

summary: HENRY SCHEIN INC updated its corporate governance structure on May 31, 2018, following shareholder approval at the Annual Meeting. The changes included aligning special meeting provisions with bylaws, adjusting voting standards to reflect voting power, and moving advance notice requirements to the bylaws. The amendments also reflected new communication technologies and conformed to Delaware law. Additionally, the company adopted Section 141(c)(2) of the Delaware General Corporation Law for board committees, added procedures for shareholder meetings, and permitted electronic communications. HENRY SCHEIN, INC. approved amendments to its Certificate of Incorporation and re-elected BDO USA, LLP as its independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending December 29, 2018. The proposal received 129,258,366 votes in favor, 4,080,116 against, 203,414 abstentions, and 8,964,014 broker non-votes. The 2017 executive compensation plan was also approved by non-binding vote with 126,596,385 votes in favor, 6,433,719 against, 511,792 abstentions, and 8,964,014 broker non-votes.

summary: Brookfield Asset Management Inc. announced on June 1, 2018, that it has determined the quarterly dividend on its floating rate Cumulative Class A Preference Shares, Series 25 (TSX: BAM.PR.S). The dividend is paid at an annual rate of 2.30% over the annual yield on three-month Government of Canada treasury bills, calculated for each quarter. The company declared a quarterly dividend rate of 0.9074% (3.6% annualized) for the period July 1, 2018 to September 30, 2018, with a dividend of $0.22685 per share payable on September 28, 2018. The company is a leading global alternative asset manager with approximately US$285 billion in assets under management.

summary: On February 22, 2013, Geospace Technologies Corporation (GEOSPACE) entered into a Third Amendment to the Loan Agreement dated March 2, 2011, and a Note Modification, Renewal and Extension Agreement. The Third Amendment reflects the new legal names and internal structure of the Company and its subsidiary guarantors following an internal restructuring. It also adds swap agreements entered into by the Company or any subsidiary guarantor with the lender to the definition of Loan Documents and includes the debt arising under such swap agreements in the definition of Indebtedness. The Note Extension extends the maturity date of the Revolving Promissory Note executed in connection with the 2011 Loan Agreement to March 2, 2015. The amendments modify the definitions of Indebtedness and Loan Documents to include various hedge and exchange agreements. The complete text of the Third Amendment and Note Extension is filed as Exhibits 10.1 and 10.2, respectively, and is incorporated by reference into this report.

title: Guidance miss, audit probe could spell rough day for Hain Celestial stock
summary: Hain Celestial Group experienced a significant drop in its stock price on Tuesday, with shares plunging 27 percent after the company delayed the release of its fiscal 2016 financial results, missed guidance, and announced potential accounting concerns. The stock is on track for its worst day in history, having already lost $1.6 billion in market cap. The company identified concessions granted to certain U.S. distributors during its fiscal fourth quarter ended in June and is evaluating whether the revenue associated with these concessions was recorded in the correct period. The company also mentioned it is reviewing its internal control over financial reporting. Analysts have mixed reactions, with some calling the drop a potential buying opportunity, while others have downgraded the stock. Hain has not disclosed the names of the distributors in question and has postponed releasing its financial results until an audit committee review is completed. The company had previously forecast sales between $2.95 billion and $2.97 billion and earnings per share between $2 and $2.04, but now expects to miss these targets. Analysts like Amit Sharma believe the company's position in the health and wellness sector remains strong, while others like Phil Terpolilli suggest the accounting issues could take six to 12 months to resolve. The stock of Hain Celestial may face a challenging day due to a guidance miss and an ongoing audit probe. Analysts have expressed concerns, with one stating there are currently 'more questions than answers.' The analyst, Phil Lazar, mentioned that while it is not typically their preference to downgrade a stock on a day when it is expected to be weak, the uncertainty surrounding the potential outcomes and time frame of the review has led them to take this course of action. Lazar also noted that there is no guarantee the outcome will be materially unfavorable, and it could simply be a matter of timing. The article was revised to correct the spelling of Phil Terpolilli's last name.

summary: Nordic American Tankers Limited completed the acquisition of Scandic American Shipping Ltd. on January 11, 2013, as announced on December 17, 2012. NAT acquired 100% of Scandic's shares from a company controlled by Herbjørn Hansson, NAT's Chairman and CEO, and his family. NAT issued 1,910,112 common shares to the seller, subject to a one-year lock-up agreement. Following the acquisition, Mr. Hansson and his family own approximately 5.6% or 3.1 million shares of NAT's outstanding shares. The acquisition aligns their interests more closely with NAT's operations. The text includes a cautionary statement regarding forward-looking statements, highlighting uncertainties and risks associated with future performance and outcomes. Key factors affecting the company include global economic conditions, market fluctuations, changes in demand, operating expenses, regulatory changes, and potential litigation.

summary: The document titled 'j3101406k.htm' is a Form 6-K filing by Royal Bank of Canada, published on March 11, 2014. It outlines the issuance of Senior Global Medium-Term Notes, Series F, including $1,000,000,000 of 2.150% Senior Notes and $650,000,000 of Senior Floating Rate Notes, both due on March 15, 2019. The filing includes legal opinions from Sullivan & Cromwell LLP and Norton Rose Fulbright Canada LLP regarding the validity of the notes and tax matters. The report is incorporated by reference into the Bank’s Registration Statement on Form F-3 (File No. 333-189888). The filing is signed by James Salem, Executive Vice-President and Treasurer of Royal Bank of Canada.

summary: On January 13, 2014, SAP AG, a German-based company, filed a Form 6-K with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The filing included a press release announcing SAP's preliminary financial results for the fourth quarter and full year ended December 31, 2013. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference. The document highlights that certain non-IFRS financial measures are disclosed, which are not prepared in accordance with IFRS and should be considered alongside, not as substitutes for, traditional financial performance metrics. The report also includes forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. SAP does not undertake any obligation to update these statements. The filing is part of SAP's compliance with U.S. securities regulations. This document is a Form 6-K filing by SAP AG, dated January 13, 2014. It includes a press release dated January 10, 2014, and signatures from Christoph Huetten and Sonja Simon, both in official capacities. The filing is related to the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and is part of SAP AG's regulatory reporting obligations. The press release is listed as Exhibit 99.1 and is dated January 10, 2014. The filing is a standard corporate disclosure document and does not contain any specific financial results or market-moving information.

summary: On July 25, 2013, the U.S. Department of the Treasury recognized exceptional development projects and initiatives undertaken by the Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs) at the second annual Development Impact Honors ceremony. The event, held in Washington, brought together leaders from MDBs, Members of Congress, development and business community leaders, and senior administration officials to celebrate excellence in development. The projects honored reflect efforts to strengthen communities and advance American economic and security interests globally. Secretary Jacob J. Lew highlighted the importance of these projects, emphasizing their role in promoting clean energy, women’s economic equality, food security, and support for vulnerable populations. The projects were evaluated based on effectiveness, quality of work, and success in overcoming development challenges. Notable projects included the Cote d’Ivoire Project, which addressed gender-based violence through integrated services and community engagement, and the Uganda Community Agricultural Infrastructure Program, which improved rural infrastructure and economic opportunities. The Bhutan Green Power Project, supported by the Asian Development Bank, exemplifies sustainable development initiatives that align with U.S. priorities. The U.S. Department of the Treasury recognized multilateral development banks (MDBs) at its annual awards ceremony, highlighting their critical role in promoting economic growth, rural development, and environmental protection. One notable project was Bhutan’s collaboration with the private sector to create a run-of-the-river hydropower facility, which replaced fossil fuel-generated power with clean energy sources. The project extended hydroelectricity grids to over 8,700 rural households and facilities and introduced solar power systems to electrify schools, health clinics, and community centers in remote areas. Another initiative was the Mexico Training and Employment Program, Phase II, led by the Inter-American Development Bank. This program addressed the gap between training programs and employer needs by involving private employers in on-the-job training. From 2010 to 2012, it provided stipends to hundreds of thousands of people, helped secure employment for 1.5 million, and created a platform for job and training searches. The project also focused on vulnerable groups, including women, youth, and disabled workers. The Post-Earthquake Assessment Project in Haiti, led by the World Bank Group, showcased the role of MDBs in disaster response. The 2010 earthquake caused massive destruction, and the project aimed to restore basic services by assessing buildings, collecting damage data, and strengthening national institutions. Over 400,000 buildings were evaluated at a cost of $10 per building, facilitating safe reoccupation and recovery.

summary: Royal Bank of Canada, along with other Canadian banks and life insurance companies, issued a joint statement regarding changes to annual meeting planning. The statement highlights proactive measures taken in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including obtaining a court order to hold annual meetings via electronic means. The health and well-being of employees, clients, investors, and communities are emphasized as a collective priority.

title: Chinese President Xi Jinping speaks at Boao Forum for Asia
summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping addressed the Boao Forum for Asia, emphasizing China's commitment to opening up its economy. He announced plans to lower tariffs on automobiles and other products, as well as to enforce legal intellectual property protections for foreign firms. This announcement came on the same day the World Trade Organization reported that China filed a complaint against President Donald Trump's tariffs on imported steel and aluminum. Xi also highlighted China's intention to increase imports and achieve a more balanced international payments structure. He called for developed countries to stop imposing unfair trade restrictions on high-tech products and to relax export controls. In his speech, Xi promoted a vision of China as a global leader advocating for open systems and multilateral cooperation. He urged countries to reject zero-sum games and power politics, instead focusing on openness, connectivity, and mutual benefits. China's President Xi Jinping also mentioned the need to strengthen law enforcement related to intellectual property and encourage technological exchanges between Chinese and foreign enterprises. Regarding the Belt and Road Initiative, Xi downplayed any geopolitical ambitions, stating that the project aims to benefit the world rather than create exclusionary blocs. He reiterated that China has no geopolitical calculations and does not impose business deals on others.

summary: Optical Cable Corporation (“OCC”) was awarded a contract to supply its proprietary products to a major defense contractor for the U.S. Department of Defense. The contract includes a purchase order totaling more than $1.0 million. The Company expects to begin manufacturing the products in the fiscal third quarter of 2021 and continue throughout fiscal year 2021. Further details regarding the contract were not disclosed.

summary: SAP SE, a multinational software company, announced that the Executive Board and the Supervisory Board recommend shareholders approve a dividend of €1.85 per share for the fiscal year 2020 at the Annual General Meeting of Shareholders. The announcement was made in a press release issued on February 25, 2021. The document also mentioned that two by-elections of shareholder representatives in the SAP Supervisory Board will be held at the 2021 Annual General Meeting of Shareholders. The press release included forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties that could affect SAP's future financial results. The information is provided in compliance with U.S. securities regulations and is part of SAP's filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

title: Noble Group flags $5 billion annual loss, races to strike debt deal
summary: Noble Group, a troubled commodities trader, warned of a massive annual loss of $4.78 billion to $4.98 billion, citing challenging operating conditions. The company is racing to finalize a $3.4 billion debt-for-equity swap to ensure its survival. Noble announced a deal with creditors last month to halve its senior debt and give them 70 percent of the company, while existing equity holders would see their stake diluted to 10 percent. The company expects a total net loss of $1.72 billion to $1.92 billion for the quarter ending December 2017, stemming largely from non-cash losses from its mark-to-market derivatives portfolio. Noble's chairman, Paul Brough, said the company is looking forward to the final phase of its restructuring, aiming to create a new Noble as a focused and appropriately financed group set to capitalize on the high-growth Asian commodities sector. Noble also mentioned that the Ad Hoc Group, a group of senior creditors, held about 36 percent of the company's senior bonds and loans, with additional support from creditors holding about 15 percent of the senior debt instruments.

summary: Impac Mortgage Holdings, Inc. (IMPAC MORTGAGE HOLDINGS INC) suspended all lending activity for two weeks starting March 30, 2020, due to liquidity constraints and de-risking mandates from capital market counterparties. The decision followed uncertainty from a whole loan investor’s lack of communication and potential breach of its purchase commitment. The Company closed its TBA hedge position on March 18, 2020, collecting full net margin from TBA counterparties. It has not used the TBA market for hedging since then. The Company expects its capital market counterparties to fulfill obligations under contracts related to warehouse and repurchase funding, and forward sale of loans. If any counterparty fails, the Company will pursue remedies including specific performance and damages. The novel coronavirus outbreak continues to have a real-time impact on all business sectors. The company has volunteered to cover employees' health and medical benefits during the furlough period. The rapid development and fluidity of the effects of the coronavirus precludes any prediction as to the ultimate adverse impact on its business.

events.quote: The Company has instituted a two week temporary suspension of all lending activity effective as of the opening of business today, March 30, 2020.
The Company’s unrestricted cash position as of the close of business on March 27, 2020 was approximately $80 million.
increased competition in the mortgage lending industry by larger or more efficient companies

summary: Tucson Electric Power Company (TEP) completed a formal appraisal procedure with three appraisers to determine the fair market value purchase price of Springerville Unit 1, as per lease agreements. The lease agreements state that the determined purchase price will be final and binding. TEP filed a petition in the United States District Court for the District of Arizona to confirm an appraisal of $159 million for lease interests. The petition names owner participants and trustees as respondents. TEP argues the appraisal was conducted properly and seeks judicial confirmation as an arbitration award. Owner participants oppose the petition, claiming the appraisal failed to meet required standards and that TEP has not exercised its purchase option. They request the court dismiss the case, arguing no controversy exists. TEP intends to pursue legal remedies to confirm the appraisal results.

title: SEC.gov | SEC Proposes Offering Reforms for Business Development Companies and Registered Closed-End Funds
summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) proposed offering reforms for Business Development Companies (BDCs) and Registered Closed-End Funds, aiming to improve access to capital and investor communications. These reforms are part of implementing provisions from the Small Business Credit Availability Act and the Economic Growth, Regulatory Relief, and Consumer Protection Act. The changes would streamline registration processes, allowing eligible funds to use a short-form registration statement for selling securities. Funds would also be able to qualify as Well-Known Seasoned Issuers (WKSIs), benefiting from flexible registration and communication processes. The proposal includes new reporting and structured data requirements, as well as a modernized approach to registration fee payments for interval funds. The reforms are intended to align these funds with operating companies, enhancing transparency and investor access. The SEC has proposed reforms aimed at modernizing the offering process for Business Development Companies (BDCs) and Registered Closed-End Funds. These reforms would allow affected funds to utilize many of the communication rules currently available to operating companies, including the use of a 'free writing prospectus,' factual business information, forward-looking statements, and broker-dealer research reports. Funds would also be able to satisfy their final prospectus delivery obligations by filing the prospectus with the Commission. Interval funds would register an indefinite number of shares and pay registration fees based on net issuance, similar to mutual funds and exchange-traded funds. Structured data requirements would involve the use of Inline XBRL for registration statement information, as well as financial statement information for BDCs. Funds filing Form 24F-2 would need to submit the form in XML format. Periodic reporting requirements would include key prospectus disclosure in annual reports and management’s discussion of fund performance (MDFP). Current reporting requirements would involve filing Form 8-K for material changes to investment objectives or policies and material write-downs of significant investments. Incorporation by reference would require affected funds to make materials available on a website instead of providing copies to new purchasers. The comment period for the proposal will be open for 60 days following publication in the Federal Register.

title: SC1-#4717350-v1-Comments_to_CFO_8-K_8_8_2018_v1 compared with SC1-#4717350-v3-Comments_to_CFO_8-K_8_8_2018_v1
summary: DISH Network Corporation through its subsidiary American II acquired 80% of Northstar Manager’s Class B Common Interests for $312 million. DISH owns 97% of Northstar Spectrum’s Class B Common Interests, with Northstar Manager holding 3%. Northstar Manager did not exercise its Put Right during the First Put Window (2020–2021), retaining the right to do so in the Second Put Window (2021–2022). Northstar Wireless, a subsidiary of Northstar Spectrum, participated in Auction 97 and received 261 AWS-3 Licenses in 2015. The FCC ruled in 2020 that Northstar Wireless and SNR Wireless remain under DISH Network’s de facto control, prompting appeals to the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals. The transaction did not alter existing arrangements between Northstar parties, except for ownership percentages.

summary: J.C. Penney reported mixed second-quarter results for Q2 2019, with sales declining faster than expected and falling short of analyst forecasts. The company recorded a net loss of $48 million, or 15 cents per share, compared to a loss of $101 million, or 32 cents per share, in the same period the previous year. Excluding one-time items, the loss was 18 cents per share, better than the forecast of 31 cents. However, revenue dropped 7.4% to $2.62 billion, below the expected $2.69 billion. Sales at stores open for at least a year fell 9%, worse than the anticipated 5.2% decline. The company attributed the drop to the discontinuation of appliance and furniture sales. J.C. Penney also announced a partnership with ThredUp, a secondhand retailer, and has been closing stores as part of its restructuring efforts. The company has $1.7 billion in liquidity and aims to maintain at least $1.5 billion for the year. It also reduced inventory by 12.5% and improved its cost of goods sold due to lower permanent markdowns. The retail sector faces challenges as consumers shift to online shopping and direct-to-consumer models. J.C. Penney reported its Q2 2019 earnings, revealing that the company faced delisting risks from the New York Stock Exchange due to its stock price falling below $1. On July 19, its shares dropped below the $1 threshold and continued to trade below that level, hitting an all-time low of 53 cents. However, on Thursday, shares rose more than 8%, trading at around 62 cents. The company stated its intention to increase its share price through improved operating performance or other revenue streams. As of Wednesday's close, shares had declined over 37% since January, resulting in a market value of approximately $181 million. The company has six months to comply with NYSE rules to avoid delisting.

title: Elliott Sets Up Gigamon for Speed Dating
summary: Elliott Management Corp., an activist investor focused on undervalued technology companies, has continued its strategy by acquiring a 15.3 percent stake in Gigamon Inc. in 2016. This move signaled Elliott's intent to push for a strategic review, potentially leading to a sale. Following the announcement, Gigamon's shares increased by 17 percent. Elliott has previously succeeded in pushing for the sales of Lifelock Inc. and Mentor Graphics Corp., demonstrating its effectiveness in influencing corporate decisions through activist investing.

events.quote: Elliott Management Corp., the activist investor with a penchant for undervalued technology companies, is at it again.
Elliott on Monday unveiled a 15.3 percent stake in Gigamon Inc.
The Santa Clara, California-based company's shares soared 17 percent in response.

title: FRB: FEDS Notes
summary: On August 1, 2014, the Federal Reserve Board (FRB) released FEDS Notes outlining the Enhanced Financial Accounts (EFAs) project. This initiative aims to significantly improve the Financial Accounts of the United States by providing more detailed and timely data on financial intermediation. The EFAs project includes larger-scale changes such as higher-frequency information and more-disaggregated data, even if these data are not fully integrated into the existing structure. The Financial Accounts, previously known as the Flow of Funds Accounts, are U.S. national accounts published quarterly by the FRB. They provide macro-financial flows and balance sheets for major sectors like households, financial institutions, and governments. The project also aims to enhance the usability of the Financial Accounts by improving data reporting and providing additional documentation. The EFAs project is part of the FRB's ongoing effort to improve financial accounting practices and better understand economic relationships. The FRB has outlined plans to significantly enhance the Financial Accounts to provide more detailed information on financial instruments and risk exposures. The Enhanced Financial Accounts (EFA) Project aims to improve the detail, dimensionality, and scope of the Financial Accounts by offering data at higher frequencies, more disaggregated levels, and for both market and book values. The project includes expanding information on financial derivatives, which are crucial for transferring market, credit, interest-rate, and exchange-rate risks. The enhancements will be integrated into the core of the Financial Accounts for some sectors, while others will be presented as supplementary data. The FRB is also exploring ways to improve data dissemination and communication about the Financial Accounts, including the use of new tools and analysis. These changes are intended to provide analysts and researchers with more detailed insights into the financial system.

summary: On February 26, 2021, Insperity, Inc. announced the retirement of Jay E. Mincks, Executive Vice President of Sales and Marketing. Mr. Mincks will voluntarily resign his position as an officer effective March 31, 2021. He will continue to receive the same compensation until his retirement on September 1, 2021. The Company and Mr. Mincks have entered into a consulting agreement effective September 2, 2021, with a three-year term that may be terminated earlier after the second year. Under the agreement, Mr. Mincks will provide advice and expertise on sales and marketing matters, receive $20,000 per month, and agree not to engage in competing activities or solicit certain employees until the end of the second year following the agreement's expiration or termination.

summary: On March 22, 2018, the Board of Directors of Blonder Tongue Laboratories, Inc. (BLONDER) amended and restated Article IV, Section 8 of the Company's bylaws. The original provision stated that the President would serve as the chief operating officer. The amendment allows the Board additional flexibility in defining the roles and responsibilities of senior management. The change became effective immediately upon approval by the Board. No other changes to the bylaws were made. The amendment is filed as Exhibit 3.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated by reference. The amendment does not affect the Company's financial statements or operations directly, but it reflects a shift in governance structure to enhance management flexibility.

title: 10 Businesses That Got Killed by the Internet
summary: Sears and GameStop are examples of companies negatively impacted by the rise of the internet. Sears, once the world's largest retailer, faced significant debt and declining sales due to competition from Walmart, Target, and Home Depot. Its merger with Kmart worsened its financial situation. GameStop, which specialized in video game sales, reported a $673 million loss in the previous year and faces potential bankruptcy by late 2019. Both companies struggled to adapt to online retail competition. Digital sales now account for 83% of total video game purchases, according to the Entertainment Software Association. This shift in buying habits has disrupted GameStop's "buy back and resell" business model, resulting in weak earnings and a grim prognosis for the brand.

title: Black Friday shoppers spend record $7.4 billion
summary: Black Friday online sales reached $7.4 billion in 2019, according to Adobe Analytics, marking the second largest online shopping day ever, behind last year's Cyber Monday, which reached $7.9 billion. The average order value per consumer, at $168, was up nearly 6% year-over-year and set a new Black Friday record. Adobe Analytics measures transactions from 80 of the top 100 U.S. online retailers. "Small Business Saturday" has already seen $470 million in online spend, up 18% over last year, as of 9 a.m. ET. Sales are on pace to surpass $3 billion for the day, said Adobe. Online sales are up about 20% from last year, according to Adobe. The jump in cyber activity is a sign consumers are becoming more comfortable buying larger items at discount prices without going to the store. Adobe is still expecting spending on Cyber Monday this year to hit an even bigger record $9.4 billion, an 18.9% jump from a year ago. Shoppers have already spent $4.2 billion online on Thanksgiving Day, a 14.5% increase from last year and a record high, Adobe said Friday. Some of the most popular purchased items include Disney's "Frozen 2" toys, video games such as FIFA 20 and Madden 20, and electronics such as Apple Airpods and Samsung TVs. While some traditional brick-and-mortar stores have successfully transitioned to online shopping, such as Target and Walmart, others including Kohl's, Gap and Macy's have struggled. Target's stock has risen about 95% this year and Walmart has surged nearly 30% while Kohl's, Gap and Macy's shares are down 25% or more year to date.

summary: On March 1, 2016, SanDisk Corporation issued a press release announcing that it had issued notices to holders of its outstanding 1.5% Convertible Senior Notes due 2017 and 0.5% Convertible Senior Notes due 2020 regarding an anticipated Designated Event and Fundamental Change. The notices were sent to holders of these notes, and copies of the press release and notices were attached to the Form 8-K filing. The announcement was part of SanDisk's communication regarding potential changes that could affect the terms of the notes. The document also includes forward-looking statements about the proposed merger and its implications for the company's business and industry. This document is an 8-K filing by SanDisk Corporation dated March 1, 2016, which outlines forward-looking statements related to a proposed merger with Western Digital's subsidiary, Schrader Acquisition Corporation. The filing highlights the potential benefits of the merger and the expected closing date. However, it also emphasizes the risks and uncertainties associated with the merger, including the possibility of not obtaining stockholder approvals, regulatory delays, integration challenges, and potential adverse effects on business relationships. The document warns that these forward-looking statements are not guarantees of future results and are subject to various risks. The filing also notes that the risks associated with the merger are more fully discussed in the joint proxy statement/prospectus included in the Registration Statement on Form S-4 filed with the SEC. The forward-looking statements in this document are only as of the date of the particular statement, and neither SanDisk nor Western Digital undertakes any obligation to revise or update them. SanDisk Corporation announced on March 1, 2016, that it had entered into a conversion agreement for its 0.5% Convertible Senior Notes due 2020. The filing indicates that the conversion process was anticipated and that the terms were set forth in the agreement. This event is significant for the holders of the notes as it affects their potential conversion into equity. The event is relevant to the company's capital structure and shareholder equity, and it may impact the company's financial position and stock price. Additionally, SanDisk Corporation filed an 8-K on March 1, 2016, announcing a proposed merger with Western Digital. The filing includes information about the transaction, which will be submitted to the stockholders of both companies. Western Digital filed a Registration Statement on Form S-4 with the SEC, which was declared effective on February 5, 2016. The joint proxy statement/prospectus is being provided to the stockholders of both companies. Investors are urged to read the documents carefully as they contain important information about the proposed merger. The documents can be accessed on the SEC's website and the websites of SanDisk and Western Digital.

summary: The Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee (TBAC) of the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association convened on August 1st, 2017, in a closed session at the Hay Adams Hotel. All members, except Michelle Neal, were present. Counselor to the Secretary Craig Phillips, Fiscal Assistant Secretary David Lebryk, Acting Assistant Secretary for Financial Markets Monique Rollins, Director of the Office of Debt Management Fred Pietrangeli, and Deputy Director of the Office of Debt Management John Dolan welcomed the Committee. Other Treasury staff members present included Dave Chung, Ken Phelan, Jared Roscoe, Rozlyn Engel, Tom Katzenbach, Chris Cameron, Mike Puglia, Renee Tang, Brandon Taylor, and Elisha Whipkey. Federal Reserve Bank of New York staff members Lorie Logan, Nathaniel Wuerffel, and Nick Steele were also present. Director Pietrangeli discussed key takeaways, including a forecast of $501 billion in net marketable borrowing for FY 2018 Q1, assuming the debt limit will be increased. He also noted the Federal Reserve’s clarity on balance sheet normalization and its implications for Treasury borrowing needs. The Committee then considered various issuance scenarios to fund SOMA redemptions, with members discussing tradeoffs in different strategies, including costs, flexibility, and the impact on weighted average maturity (WAM). The Committee adjourned at 12:30 p.m. for lunch and reconvened at 1:30 p.m. to continue the discussion. The TBAC meeting on August 1, 2017, discussed the timing of Treasury's strategy decision, suggesting it should be made as early as the November refunding but no later than the first calendar quarter of 2018. The discussion on potential issuance choices and the potential for sizable bill issuance prompted a discussion on the weighted average maturity (WAM). The Committee generally agreed that WAM should remain about the same or increase moving forward. Some members referenced a presentation from the May 2017 TBAC meeting, which suggested that the marginal benefits of extending WAM past the intermediate sector were very low. Other members cautioned about using WAM as a metric for cost and risk. The Committee agreed to discuss the topic of WAM, issuance models, and additional portfolio metrics at some future point. A Committee member also presented findings from a model on the potential effects of balance sheet normalization on other risk assets. The Committee adjourned at 2:45 p.m.
